members.name: Return contract: value or null, with coverage count
members.problem: A missing or crashed agent result must never be read as 'nothing found'.
members.mechanism: Every run resolves to a value or null. The script returns results, missing, not_started, halted slice and coverage; G1 re-runs or waives each gap in writing and coverage must read 16/16 or carry waivers.
members.status_note: Rule at G1; W1 later reported 16/16 coverage (see staged workflow record).
members.results: Not yet tested as a rule; W1 reported 16/16 coverage [M].

members.name: Models give verdicts; code computes counts and scores
members.problem: Holistic 1-100 model scores are unreliable and humans cannot read all logic; a script that filters, slices or asks a model to count can lose items without trace.
members.mechanism: Models give binary or enum verdicts; code computes the score, with coverage from Object.keys(out).length, logged dropped counts and no silent caps; each phase has a cheap human-checkable proof (Done-when checks, CI, fail-before/pass-after tests).
members.status_note: Already program law; optional extra: report received and kept counts for any filtering step.
members.results: Confirmed rule.
members.aka: B-06, R-05, G4-F147, G4-F154, counts computed in code, no silent caps

members.name: Gate-script hygiene: tagged run() results
members.problem: A schema-exhaustion failure could look like a usage-limit null, so the breaker may trip for the wrong reason; scripts can also give a skeptic contaminating inputs or trust an agent's own list of reads.
members.mechanism: Wrap agent calls so a result is tagged null (agent died), a caught error with message, or a value; a pure skeptic-input function; compare self-listed reads with the transcript; rename a verdict field 'reasoning' to 'explanation'.
members.status_note: Trial, unrefuted (one Sonnet pass plus judgement); refuters downgraded all four to FixFlow-only: no dead reviewer read as clean and no contaminated reviewer is on the testbed record. Open precondition: what agent() returns on schema exhaustion.
members.results: not yet tested here.
members.aka: S-1, S-4, S-5, I-13, Workflow-script hygiene borrows from BAML

members.name: Rename VERDICT.reasoning to explanation
members.problem: A required 'reasoning' field in the skeptic's verdict can trigger a reasoning_extraction refusal: a billed reply whose output may not match the schema, costing a verdict.
members.mechanism: First grep committed transcripts of G2's twelve skeptics and seven lost refuters for stop_reason refusal (zero tokens). Then rename the field to explanation at the next section 5.2 edit.
members.status_note: Survived the refuter as one of four trials; not applied. Ordered cheapest first.
members.results: Not yet tested. G2 got all 12 skeptic verdicts back, so no refusal is on record.

members.name: Add description keywords to the output schemas
members.problem: The section 5.2 schemas carry no description, so P0-P3 are defined nowhere and limits such as 300 words live only in JS comments the model never sees. G2 saw eight of twelve skeptic verdicts lower a severity.
members.mechanism: One Sonnet probe checks whether a schema property description reaches the model. If so, define each P-level and verdict value once in a shared constant, then compare analyst-vs-skeptic severity agreement.
members.status_note: One of four surviving trials; BAML-specific rendering evidence judged not to transfer.
members.results: Not yet tested. Baseline to beat: G2 eight of twelve skeptic verdicts lowered a severity [M]; 4 of 12 survived [M].

members.name: One constants table for verdict enums and buckets
members.problem: A verdict value could be added to a schema enum without a matching bucket in the gate script, leaving results unclassified.
members.mechanism: One table generates both the schema enums and the bucket mapping, with citation statuses folded in. About 15 lines.
members.status_note: Trial, unrefuted.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Short, capped agent hand-backs and hygiene rules
members.problem: The main session fills with whole-document reads, long subagent reports and rewritten files; subagent file writes were believed refused, so long reports pass through the orchestrator.
members.mechanism: Agents return text capped in size: about 2,500 characters with path:line evidence, 400-character notes, at most 40 facts of 200 characters; command agents log noisy output to files and return tails and exit codes; drops are logged, never silent; big files come from a script.
members.status_note: Clinic returns-as-text rule in use (400-character figure is a stated property, not measured); hygiene rules file built but not enforced or installed; FixFlow W1 caps designed. Superseded in part by results-on-disk, since the write refusal was an unchecked report.
members.results: Not yet tested. Forensics motivating the rules: one script rewritten in full twice (24k and 25k characters) (M). No token figures.
members.aka: A5-06, A8-16, no silent caps, Context-hygiene habits, Output discipline: caps with logged drops, Compact typed subagent returns

members.name: Specialist refute-by-default reviewers (offline sync, migrations, security)
members.problem: The hand-rolled offline engine, populated-table migrations and security-sensitive code each have FixFlow-specific invariants; generic checklists miss them or tell agents to 'fix' deliberate behaviour (such as the lock that blocks a correct PIN).
members.mechanism: Three sourced skills with paired Opus reviewer agents: offline-sync (outbox contract, never delete a queued write), fastapi-alembic-safety (NOT VALID then VALIDATE, never downgrade), appsec-review-asvs (OWASP ASVS 5.0 / MASVS 2.1 with listed deviations). Each runs fixed commands only and never probes a live host.
members.status_note: Skills and Opus agents on draft PR #185, not merged.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Turn skills into pinned project agents
members.problem: Subagents lack domain knowledge (Android background work, Odoo, recovery, security review), and skills fetched from outside must reach the agents that use them at the right price tier without every session loading everything by hand.
members.mechanism: Each sourced skill is distilled into .claude/agents/<name>.md (system prompt, tool list, pinned model). Workflows or sessions call it by agentType / subagent_type. Skills the main session loads itself live in .claude/skills/<name>/. Priority 1: Android background, field debugging, recovery ops, Odoo API.
members.status_note: Designed in the orchestration document (then awaiting the owner's skills research); since applied to 11 fixflow-* agent definitions on draft PR #185, which is not merged. No run results yet.
members.results: Not yet tested; no run results in either source.
members.aka: Wiring plan, skills for subagents, section 9 skills list, design §9 wiring rule

members.name: Model tiers by role, raise effort before tier
members.problem: Model choice per agent is the main cost lever; the strongest model should be spent only where mistakes are expensive and cheap models do literal work, and nobody should run at an unchosen strength.
members.mechanism: Haiku extracts into closed schemas; Sonnet maps, researches, runs gates, checks citations; Opus analyses, refutes, owns invariant-sensitive code; Fable briefs, gates and judges. Model and effort named on every start; raise effort before moving up a tier; agents never told their tier.
members.status_note: Used in FixFlow W1/W2/review and the whole clinic build (one mid-run change, S09 Sonnet to Opus); built as 6 Opus, 5 Sonnet, 1 Haiku agent definitions on PR #185.
members.results: W1 mix 4 Haiku, 9 Sonnet, 3 Sonnet-web [M design]. Clinic: no token or cost measurement of tiering; every slice still needed 2-4 review rounds. Tier chosen by slice type, not validated against defect rates.
members.aka: Tier guide, routing rule, model routing, A1-01, design section 3 routing

members.name: Route by model tier, window and price
members.problem: Model choice might be assumed to drive token use, yet a cheaper model with a bigger window can cost more tokens through larger re-read contexts; reading code cannot settle thin-evidence questions.
members.mechanism: Choose the model for slice work by window size as well as price; spend Opus xhigh only where evidence is thin over cheap maps; verification bought only where it moves the plan. Routing changes the rate per token, not the count.
members.status_note: The token report names model mix as NOT the bottleneck for token count; routing by window is a comparison across models doing different work, not a trial; Opus-where-thin is a design rationale to review after W2 spend.
members.results: Opus 65% of calls and 52% of tokens; Fable 6.5% of calls and 16%; Sonnet 28% and 32% (M). Slice calls on Sonnet read 1,452 million (M) tokens; on Opus 1,306 million (M) in nearly twice the calls.
members.aka: model mix, routing by price, model routing by window, Why this shape

members.name: Escalation ladder: Sonnet, then Opus, then Fable
members.problem: A hard new problem is the point, not a weakness: the cheap model will fail some work outright and the average gap between tiers hides that hard tail.
members.mechanism: Cheap model tries first; a caught failure gets one cheap retry, then Opus, then Fable. The problem is solved once at the lowest tier that can, and the solution is stored.
members.status_note: Modelled with fixed order and one gate; real sessions skip rungs, repeat them, or end with the owner.
members.results: Model at middle values: 25.7 [G] cost per piece, 21.2% [G] wrong, against strong model directly 29.9 [G] and 11.2% [G]. Real cases: ladder step 'not reached' in 23 [M], 'works' in 3 [M]; higher tier was not the catcher in 12 [M].

members.name: Keep Haiku prompts under about 100k input tokens
members.problem: Past a certain input size Haiku's price steps up, removing its cost advantage on large dumps.
members.mechanism: Keep each Haiku extraction prompt under about 100k input tokens and split large dumps; use Haiku only for literal or name-varying extraction into typed schemas, never inference.
members.status_note: Stated as a rule in the tier table.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Agent file: pinned model, tools, preloaded skill
members.problem: A subagent inherits the session's model and loads nothing unless told; its role, price tier and tool access must be fixed in one file.
members.mechanism: Frontmatter sets name, description, tools, model (haiku, sonnet or opus), skills (preloads the full SKILL.md, up to 32) and effort where the design pins it. The body is the system prompt: read-only unless told, cite everything, return a named schema.
members.status_note: 11 fixflow-* definitions plus fixflow-explorer on draft PR #185; fields checked against code.claude.com docs on 2026-11-03.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Wave board as single current-state file
members.problem: Give one authoritative place for what is built, in review and next, so any session can pick up the build.
members.mechanism: One file, task.md: current-state table (slice, wave, status, session, branch, tier, gate), dated gate-review sections, wrap-up, next-action paragraphs and open questions. Root edits only; gate sections stay as written.
members.status_note: In use to wrap-up; header status line went stale; append-only gate sections let earlier statements go stale.
members.results: 829 lines, 219,111 bytes [M]; table rows run to several thousand characters; nothing gives the owner a live progress view (B14).

members.name: What-is-true-now view and generated board
members.problem: Slice status, verdicts and findings are re-read and go stale; shared documents have one writer, the root edits the board by hand and sessions carry a 221 KB document.
members.mechanism: Each slice writes a small state fragment; tools (never a model reading prose) generate a short board and a view of each fact with the commit it became true and the commit that superseded it; later a SQLite table. The board's diff is a local-check step.
members.status_note: Verdict: worth having. Phase 3 build in harness v2 starting as generated fragments and board; nothing built.
members.results: Not yet built or tested. Target: board from 221 KB (M) to under 20 KB (T); root edits at merge zero (T).
members.aka: temporal recall, temporal view, work-state table, validity by commit, B13

members.name: Slice state fragments and generated board
members.problem: One writer keeps an 800-line board and stale shared documents.
members.mechanism: Each slice writes a state fragment; a generator builds a short board; its diff is a check step; tests assert routing documents.
members.status_note: Build class; not built.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Temporal knowledge graph
members.problem: Remember when a fact was true (valid from one commit until superseded) and when it was recorded, so recall never returns stale conclusions.
members.mechanism: Facts stored with validity intervals and invalidation; the compile's small form is the temporal view, written only by tools.
members.status_note: Our graph test had one snapshot per commit, no validity intervals and no invalidation, so a temporal graph was not tested.
members.results: Outside study: context cut from 115k to 1.6k tokens against the full context, benchmark disputed (S). Not yet tested here.
members.aka: TKG, Graphiti or Zep style, bi-temporal edges

members.name: Model-built knowledge graph and graph database
members.problem: Capture semantic relations that parsers miss (meaning, summaries, clusters) so an agent fetches small context fast, and find code and recall facts through a rich graph.
members.mechanism: A model reads code and docs and writes entities and relations, optionally with per-cluster summaries (GraphRAG style), possibly served from a graph database server or paired with embeddings.
members.status_note: Compile says do not build; harness v2 defers it. Our graph test used only a parser-built graph, so a knowledge graph was not tested; the owner challenged this as narrow.
members.results: Outside: model-extracted graphs cost about a thousand times vector indexing and often underperform plain retrieval (S). The one large outside gain was measured against full context and its benchmark is disputed. Not tested here.
members.aka: knowledge graph, KG, graph and memory machinery

members.name: Scheduler-system knowledge graph (Pulse)
members.problem: Candidate source of the owner's recollection of a graph-based memory.
members.mechanism: A scheduling assistant writing structured JSON episodes to a temporal graph (Graphiti on Neo4j), bypassing model extraction at write time.
members.status_note: A different project; README-level look only.
members.results: Not yet tested; no benchmark found.

members.name: W0-results.md as the single working board
members.problem: The owner and coordinator need one compiled place to see what is done, what is open and who is doing what.
members.mechanism: One file holds the P0a step table, the owner decisions table with defaults, the deploy-train table, the lane board and coordinator notes. An unknown is written 'unknown, because ...', never 0 or blank.
members.status_note: Lane board had 10 rows on 2026-11-13.
members.results: Records 8 running lanes and 2 done phases (L1, P0a-prep) (M).
members.aka: P0a step table, deploy-train table, lane board, coordinator notes

members.name: Pull-only lookup, nothing pushed or hooked
members.problem: Machinery that pushes extra context into every turn showed no measurable gain in the clinic testbed and costs tokens on every call.
members.mechanism: Agents run the ks lookup on demand; nothing is pushed or hooked. Start with a free audit and an explicit owner yes, a pilot with a kill criterion, and a stop point before any Docker, sync or wiring.
members.status_note: Evidence is about always-loaded files and a rejected error-injection hook, not a lookup hook; an edit-time hook is D21, default off.
members.results: Clinic synthetic trials showed identical acceptance with and without a context projection (M, per source). Not tested for the store itself.

members.name: Pull-only lookups with a hard output cap
members.problem: Fetched content is about 27-28.5% (E) of context and is re-read about 50 times (E) per token; always-loaded lessons tax every call. A session's own learning is carried in the window or lost in summaries.
members.mechanism: Nothing is pushed into context. A lookup prints at most one lead and one candidate within 2,000 characters (about 860 tokens), returned as a tool result mid-window so the prompt cache survives. A library holds what a session learned, fetched on demand.
members.status_note: Cap built into KS-2 and KS-3 of the knowledge-store design; unproven. Zero-token index replay first (D23). Moving CLAUDE.md stories out waits on the pilot. Library-as-external-memory is a use case, not measured.
members.results: Not yet tested. 2,000 characters measured at about 860 tokens, not 500 (M, 2,904 Bash results); subagents start above 63k prompt tokens (M). Inside one window re-reading is 0.5-1.5% (E), so any gain is across sessions; 72 paths (E) hold half the fetched tokens. Prompt caching already works: 98.2% of context sum is cache reads (M). Compaction dropped a fetched entry in 1 case, 4 went the other way (M).
members.aka: pull-only, 2,000-character cap, KS-F16, KS-P8, Ask, do not read, cache-safe index placement, Library as a session's external memory

members.name: Reasoning-cache library for cheaper models
members.problem: Most tokens run on strong, costly models, and sessions re-read the same files and re-solve solved problems. The goal is equal output from a cheaper model by reusing solutions already worked out.
members.mechanism: A separate memory of verified solutions in six SQLite tables rebuilt from a git journal. A cheap model looks up a similar solved problem, adapts and uses it; an unsolved one climbs the ladder (Sonnet, Opus, Fable) and its answer is stored. Asked, never pushed; every lookup counted.
members.status_note: Never built; modelled with guessed values (the pathway map) and designed into harness v2. Stated as unproven; nothing like it was tried in the clinic testbed. First test is a zero-token replay.
members.results: Not yet built or tested. Model at middle values: cost 1.03 [G] and wrong rate 1.01 [G] of the ladder's (parity); of 100 pieces the cheap model gets wrong, 0.35 [G] end up right (31.7 [G] at the all-good setting). Beats the ladder in 17 of 121 cells [G]. A compaction adapter on another project used 6 to 17 % [M] more tokens for the same recall.
members.aka: the library, reasoning cache, R3 The library compounds, Library, harness memory that updates itself

members.name: A ks guide command printed from command definitions
members.problem: Knowledge-store documentation could drift from the tool's real commands.
members.mechanism: ks guide prints guidance from the same command definitions, with a test that every subcommand appears.
members.status_note: Refuted: ks and its SKILL.md live in one repo and commit, so version skew cannot arise; the store is unbuilt.
members.results: Not tested.

members.name: ks command-line tool plus skill as the agent interface
members.problem: Subagents and workflow agents need one access path to the knowledge store that works with no configuration or approval prompt.
members.mechanism: A zero-dependency Node CLI called through Bash: lookup, verify, show, outcome, claim, record, close. A skill (description 300-400 characters) carries the procedure; an MCP wrapper over read verbs is optional and later.
members.status_note: No hook in v1. D15 (MCP wrapper) and D21 (edit-time hook, default off) are held.
members.results: Not yet tested. A skill description at its ceiling would add about 620 tokens per call (E).

members.name: Pull graph output, never push; build per worktree
members.problem: Stop a graph or memory layer breaking the cached start of every window and stop it describing the wrong working tree.
members.mechanism: Graph output returned only as a tool result, never in the system prompt or CLAUDE.md; graph built per worktree at query time because agents work in five worktrees with uncommitted files.
members.status_note: A rule for any future build, not itself a build.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Similarity-based reuse (a hit is a hypothesis)
members.problem: Exact repeats are rare in the record, but similar problems across projects and over time may be common; the open question is whether a similar-not-same stored solution fits.
members.mechanism: Fetch the nearest stored solution, treat the hit as a hypothesis, adapt it, and let tests decide whether it holds. Entries are verified when written.
members.status_note: Similar-problem coverage on this owner's work was never measured.
members.results: Not yet tested here. Outside: 17-45% (S) of fixes follow recurring patterns; 40% (E) of this repo's code commits fit six file shapes; similar-case retrieval raised success more than it cut tokens.

members.name: Parked-start technique
members.problem: The app only accepts a new session start on a turn the owner began, so work stops while the owner is away.
members.mechanism: On the owner's turn, pre-create dependent sessions with a brief 'PARKED START'; release each later with SendMessage once a dependency merges, because messages work on automated turns.
members.status_note: Does nothing against usage limits.
members.results: Used 6 Nov for three parked sessions (ports 55452-55454) (M). It did not prevent the 6 to 9 Nov halt.

members.name: Parked starts; lanes start in owner turns
members.problem: The orchestrator cannot start sessions unless the owner's message begins the turn; messages to a busy lane arrive only at turn end, and releasing everything at once overloads the plan limit.
members.mechanism: Create sessions on the owner's turn and release them later by message. Start lanes only in user-initiated turns; a correction to a busy lane lands as a follow-up turn.
members.status_note: In use; the 9 November release of all parked sessions at once caused a 2,030 s queue.
members.results: One wait of 2,030 s on 9 November after every session resumed at once [M].

members.name: Scheduler: two at a time, waits parked outside sessions
members.problem: After a stop every session was released at once and waited together, holding context and burning tokens; one check then waited 2,030 s.
members.mechanism: Turn the wave plan into running sessions, release at most two at a time (one new slice per five minutes in the model), keep waiting slices parked outside any session, and bring sessions back after a stop.
members.status_note: Part of the resume list and budget rule; the budget rule applies from phase 1.
members.results: Not yet tested. Record: two at a time got further, 18 of 48 agents finished in one window [M]; a lean run finished 30 of 31 [M].
members.aka: R4 The pile-up control, Parked starts

members.name: One token budget: lanes two at a time, written before launch
members.problem: Adding fresh reviewers per fix round, gate workflows, final-head reviewers and replays would recreate limit stops; a 10-lane workflow hit the five-hour limit in about 15 minutes.
members.mechanism: List everything that adds an agent with its cost; budget subagent tokens per window before launch; lanes two at a time; every step writes to disk; stop after the first empty result; lean mode with one verifier per lane; no harness agents while a FixFlow phase runs.
members.status_note: Clinic practice in use (no unattended resume; a human relaunches); applies from phase 1 of v2, phase 5 measures it. Budget figure not yet set.
members.results: Run 1: stopped after about 15 min at 2.44M subagent tokens, 2 of 19 agents done (M). Lanes two at a time: 3.4M tokens, 18 of 48 finished (M). Lean run: 30 of 31 agents on 3.28M tokens (M). One window about 3.4M subagent tokens, about 14% of weekly limit (M); October had 14 limit episodes (M).
members.aka: CR-04, One budget, token budget as numbers, Workflow sizing for plan limits

members.name: No waiting inside a session
members.problem: A waiting lane keeps its context and burns tokens; median recorded wait 409 s and longest 2,030 s.
members.mechanism: A waiting slice is parked; the check runs in the background, not a foreground polling loop.
members.status_note: Build in phase 2 (heartbeat and background checks).
members.results: Not yet tested. Median recorded wait 409 s (M); longest 2,030 s (M).

members.name: Machine-wide check lock with two slots
members.problem: Several sessions running full checks at once crashed the PC and slowed each other, then queued behind each other.
members.mechanism: An OS file lock in the git common directory shared by all worktrees, two slot files, one check per checkout, holder printed each minute, 45-minute bounded wait. The second slot opens only while 8 GiB of memory is free.
members.status_note: In use. The 8 GiB figure was a safety margin, never measured; a check's peak memory was never measured; the lock is not fair; the second slot mostly stayed closed. Three slots rejected for memory reasons.
members.results: Two overlapping checks 435 s each vs 389-418 s single, 1.8-1.9x throughput (M). With the 8 GiB gate the second slot never opened in about 980 samples (free memory 2.1-6.2 GiB); waits 3 s to 2,030 s (M).
members.aka: A3-06, A3-07, A3-08, A4-12, A8-02, two check slots, TEST_SLOTS = 2

members.name: Concurrency cap and load rules after the two shutdowns
members.problem: The PC shut down uncleanly twice under concurrent full test runs on 5 and 6 November; the cause is unknown.
members.mechanism: Cap work to three or four children and one full check at a time, enforced by a lock directory in the temp folder until the git-directory lock replaced it. On 6 Nov slots replaced the one-job rule. A sampler writes system CPU and memory each second.
members.status_note: A mitigation, not a diagnosis. The cooperative lock was retired on 6 Nov (USER-23) for two slots; the cause was never found.
members.results: Cause not diagnosed. Free memory 0.0-0.8 GiB at lows with two checks beside six sessions, 2-6 GiB with one (M). Root measured 0.4 of 24 processors busy while a check waited on the lock (M).
members.aka: A1-11, A8-07, Load rules after two unclean PC shutdowns

members.name: Memory headroom guard on the second slot
members.problem: Two simultaneous checks drove free memory to 0.0-0.8 GB, the suspected cause of unclean shutdowns.
members.mechanism: Slot 1 is offered only while 8.0 GiB of physical memory is available, re-read at every poll; unreadable means closed. The 8 GiB constant is a guess.
members.status_note: In use; collapses to one slot in practice.
members.results: About 980 samples: 8 GiB never available; free 2.1-6.2 GiB (M). Waits 647, 3, 256, 614 s. Memory is read only at admission. Per-check footprint not measured.

members.name: Weighted machine-wide slot lock for heavy jobs
members.problem: Eight lanes starting at once would exhaust the 31 GB of RAM with backend stacks, test runs, Gradle builds and emulators.
members.mechanism: ff-slot.sh gives out 3 slots (2 while a Gradle lane runs); a backend stack, Jest, Vitest or emulator takes 1, a Gradle build is exclusive. Slots are directories reaped only when the owning process is gone; a lane never starts heavy work outside it.
members.status_note: Every gate run takes a slot; refuter finding 14 changed how slots are reaped.
members.results: A backend stack used about 0.4-0.5 GB, not its 3 GB cap (M). Free RAM with eight sessions was 5.5-7.7 GB (M).

members.name: Fair first-come queue with heavy-job patience
members.problem: Waiters retried at random so one lane waited 20 minutes while later arrivals were served, and two exclusive Android builds held up eight short runs for most of an hour.
members.mechanism: Each waiter drops a ticket in a queue folder and is served in arrival order. A weight-1 job may pass a heavier job that has waited under 900 seconds; after that the heavy job blocks everyone behind it so it cannot starve.
members.status_note: Rewritten after the failures; the ticket content format is frozen.
members.results: Before: a 20 minute wait (M) and about an hour of blocking by two Android builds (M). After the fix: not yet measured.

members.name: Stub run of gate scripts (no-model test)
members.problem: A new gate or merge script could mistake a dead or failing reviewer for a clean one; bookkeeping defects were found by review, not by tests, because nothing runs a gate script without spending model tokens.
members.mechanism: Run the Workflow script body under node with stub agent/parallel/pipeline/log/phase injecting null slices, a throw, REFUTED and UNVERIFIABLE verdicts and over-cap claims; every id must appear exactly once across results, missing and not_started. About 40 lines.
members.status_note: Surviving trial; feasibility settled in one stub run (script body ran under node and returned live 2, missing b). No testbed gate script exists, so only planted cases can be run. P-10 (a stub switch) is the same idea, superseded by S-3.
members.results: Feasibility proven in one stub run (M). Not yet tested against the three recorded defects. Planned proof: null reviewer, throw, refuted verdict, reader 'none' must not reach merge.
members.aka: S-3, P-10, mechanism 5, stub harness for gate and merge scripts

members.name: Sealed replay with read log, plus stub run
members.problem: A replay of a recorded fix chain is unfair if the agent can peek at the later fix, finding tables or board; new gate scripts can also be trusted without proof.
members.mechanism: Run a recorded fix chain in a sealed clone and in a plain worktree; the read log must show zero opens of the later fix, finding tables or board. Stub-run every new gate script before trusting it.
members.status_note: Phase 3, first script, no tokens; named in the mechanisms table.
members.results: Not yet run.
members.aka: Mechanism 1, G2-F051, G2-F044, G4-F023, section 9.3 mechanisms 1 and 5, Seal on replays and stub run of gate scripts

members.name: Dry run of the gate with stand-in agents
members.problem: The gate script has no history to replay; it must be known not to let bad reviewer outputs through.
members.mechanism: Planted cases with stand-in agents: a reviewer that returns nothing, a crash, a refuted verdict, a reader of 'nobody' on a high-risk branch. None may reach merge.
members.status_note: Planted cases, not a replay; build before any real agent enters the gate.
members.results: Not yet run.

members.name: Replay seal and read log
members.problem: When an old fix chain is replayed to test a review method, the replaying agent can pass by reading the later fix or the answer; replays need to be sealed and arms need identical inputs to be fair.
members.mechanism: A clone with no later refs; the answer key hashed first and committed only after judging; a read log from the replay agent's transcript; one head commit and one hashed brief per arm, otherwise the result is reported 'not comparable'.
members.status_note: PR #186 rated G2-F051 and G4-F023 adopt and G2-F044 trial; the compile files the merged mechanism as a script at zero tokens. A proposal, never run.
members.results: not yet tested. Proof planned: one recorded fix chain run in a sealed clone and a plain worktree; the read log must show zero opens of the later fix, finding tables or board.

members.name: Brief lint and dry-run flag in scripts
members.problem: A hand-edit of a brief could drop the CONTEXT block, leak a tier word, or paste a raw schema into prose, and edits are hard to review before spending.
members.mechanism: A pure in-script lint before any agent() call, and a dry-run flag returning assembled prompts and schemas instead of calling agent().
members.status_note: Refuted: agent() already rejects bad schemas, CONTEXT is added by one concatenation, and diffing the saved script gives the text diff.
members.results: Not tested; no hand-edit regression of a brief is on record.

members.name: State kept in the repository, parents judge by diff
members.problem: Work state lived in chat context and was lost on compaction or restart; a stopped session must be resumable and parents must not trust a child's own summary.
members.mechanism: One task record per node (docs/tasks/<id>/task.md: status, next action, evidence) is the current-state index; plan, review and checkpoint are projections that cannot overrule it. Parent reads the diff and record. Resume from branch plus record.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed (37 task folders); for FixFlow the review ruled skip the task tree because state owners already exist (plan, PR body, W0-results, git).
members.results: 37 task folders [M]. No real dead-session recovery timed; resume tooling tested only on a synthetic pilot with no LLM calls. No resume time or conflict rate measured.
members.aka: A1-03, task record per node, docs/tasks/<id>/task.md, A7-01, State-owner task tree and evidence JSON, preservation manifests

members.name: One phase per session, state kept in the repo
members.problem: Late calls in a long session re-read everything before them (up to 944k tokens per call). The long-lived main window is the largest token cost, so it needs a small, steady size.
members.mechanism: Each phase of the plan starts in a fresh session with a small context; state lives in the repo and draft PR body, not the window. Lead sessions compact earlier so the main window stays near 150-200k instead of 333-396k.
members.status_note: Binding ruling HR-C1 (plan v6); state-in-repo already done; the 150-200k cap and smaller pre-read are not yet applied. Phase 5 lever 1 in harness v2.
members.results: Slice sessions are 66.4% (M) of tokens, about 306k tokens per call and about 519 calls per session. Exposure (M): 39% of FixFlow and 74% of clinic cache-read tokens sit in calls past 200k. Saving not yet tested; effect on limit stops unknown.
members.aka: HR-C1, lever 1, Session shape, one phase per new session, Cap the orchestrator window at 150-200k, Per-window token budget and slice-session caps, G1-F099, G1-F165

members.name: One phase per new session, state in the repo
members.problem: Long sessions accumulate huge windows, and state held only in a session is lost on restart.
members.mechanism: Start a new session for each phase and keep the state in files in the repo so the next session resumes from it.
members.status_note: Stated as a lesson and used as budget advice for building CureFound with agents.
members.results: Not separately measured; it is the means for lever 1.

members.name: Memory file as a pointer, not a state restatement
members.problem: The memory file carried a stale 'next step', so a new session could start from outdated state.
members.mechanism: Memory holds pointers to where state lives (plan, PR body, repository); the state itself is not restated in memory.
members.status_note: Memory rewritten in this pass.
members.results: One stale next step found and corrected (M, qualitative).

members.name: Short disciplined notes file as context memory
members.problem: Keeping what matters across compaction and restarts without heavy machinery or a restore system.
members.mechanism: A short notes file (initially blank, under 3 KiB) that the agent keeps up to date in the repo or project folder and reads to resume; it survives compaction. FixFlow already uses task.md and CLAUDE.md plus a memory index.
members.status_note: Tested in a small interrupted clinic study as the control arm; advice for CureFound agents is to skip heavy context machinery because a notes file matched it.
members.results: Matched the snapshot adapter's recall (15/15) and task 100% at 6.1 % fewer tokens (M); ordinary input 794,310 vs adapter 842,620 vs native 720,036 (M). Of 15 modelled savings, 6 were seen, all via notes that exist today (M).
members.aka: notes file, arm M, A5-12, A5-13 (control arm), agent-maintained task-notes file

members.name: Save-rule for workflow scripts, kept as run with args and brief
members.problem: Workflows are authored per task and not saved, and evidence from a run cannot be re-run or audited if the script, arguments and reviewer brief were not kept.
members.mechanism: A script is kept only after its shape has run in a second phase or answers a recorded failure. Evidence folders list the script as run plus an args JSON; each phase PR carries its Opus reviewer brief verbatim with register ids.
members.status_note: Adopt, narrowed: the 'dump every prompt' and filler-checking parts skipped.
members.results: Not yet tested. Pass: by P10 every saved script has two dated uses or a failure id; next 3 evidence folders and every phase PR from P1 comply, 3 of 3.

members.name: Save-rule and retire-check for scripts and skills
members.problem: The workflow library and the 13 skill packages can grow with scripts and skills nobody reuses.
members.mechanism: A Workflow script is kept only after its shape ran in a second phase or answers a recorded failure, with a header naming the uses. Each skill gets a retire check at the close of the phases section 9 names, by transcript grep.
members.status_note: Adopt, narrowed: calendar-based P5/P10 pruning and reopening the 13 skills were not adopted.
members.results: Not yet tested. Pass at P10 (T): each saved workflow header names at least 2 dated uses or a failure id, and each was reused at least once.

members.name: Evidence provenance and library hygiene
members.problem: Saved workflow scripts, briefs and skills can pile up without evidence they are used, and later replays cannot tell which version was run.
members.mechanism: Save each workflow script as run with its args and keep the reviewer brief verbatim; keep a script only after its shape ran in a second phase; tally skill loads per phase to retire never-firing skills.
members.status_note: G3-F088 and G3-F117 adopt, G3-F070 trial; FixFlow-only. G3-F088 downgraded: saving briefs from now on changes neither replay.
members.results: Not yet tested here.

members.name: One provenance line in each evidence README
members.problem: A later re-run or dispute of an evidence folder cannot tell which exact model and tool build produced it.
members.mechanism: Each evidence README carries one line: the session's exact model id, ids the aliases resolved to, `claude --version`, and run date. Re-measuring on every model release was refuted.
members.status_note: Adopt, narrowed to one line; per-output manifest fields and standing re-runs dropped.
members.results: not yet tested. Pass: 2 of 2 of the next evidence folders carry the line.

members.name: Skill package layout with provenance files
members.problem: Skills copied from other repos must stay traceable, licensed and small enough to load, so a maintainer can tell what was taken, changed and rejected.
members.mechanism: Each package has SKILL.md (name equals folder, description under 1024 chars, body about 400 lines), UPSTREAM.md (repo, commit SHA, paths, SPDX licence, date, Taken/Changed/Rejected), LICENSE-<upstream> verbatim, and references/. Package stays under about 150 KB.
members.status_note: Applied to all 13 packages on draft PR #185; conventions written 2026-11-03/04.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Knowledge store of solved problems (PR #183)
members.problem: The same hard defect or build trap is re-solved at an expensive model tier each time it returns, because past diagnoses live only in prose nobody can query by symptom.
members.mechanism: After a hard problem is solved, the solver records symptom, cause, failed attempts, fix, the files it depends on, and a check proving the cause is present. Later a cheap agent looks it up, runs the check, and reuses the fix; hit and miss counts decide keeping.
members.status_note: Research and design complete at v1.3.1; nothing built. Stops for the owner's yes after a free audit and again after a pilot with a kill criterion. v2 departs in three ways: work state in sibling tables, code edges added, lookup before exploring.
members.results: Not yet tested. Recurrence base rate: 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main (M, counted in the design; the v2 design states the same 3 to 5 as E). Stop rule: fewer than 3 verified hits in 20 encounters or 8 weeks [S].
members.aka: ks, the store, KS track, PR #183, knowledge store, self-evolving cache entries, self-evolving library

members.name: Write-through record at solve time, confirmed by Opus reviewer
members.problem: Entries written later from a transcript lose the diagnosis path or fill the store with junk; a self-confirmed entry could be wrong.
members.mechanism: The solving session fills a fixed schema with ks record before PR-ready, only for problems needing escalation, two failed tries or a burned build. The PR's Opus reviewer tries to refute and approves it. Cheap agents only append mechanical events.
members.status_note: Policy plus PR review, not a technical control; writer identity self-declared.
members.results: Not yet tested. Estimate: about 10-20 minutes of the solving session per record [E].
members.aka: who writes, who confirms, approver is not author

members.name: Recurrence audit before any build
members.problem: It is unproven that the same cause ever hits twice in ways a symptom-keyed store could serve, so a build could repay nothing.
members.mechanism: One Sonnet session classifies all fix commits over every ref (72, de-duplicated by patch-id), counting a repeat only if a symptom existed, git grep and CLAUDE.md could not find it, and diagnosis was non-trivial. An Opus refuter rechecks ten rows and every counted repeat.
members.status_note: No code, no install; ready whenever the owner says D1 yes.
members.results: Not yet run. Raw count already 3 to 5 same-cause repeats among 48 fix commits on main (M).

members.name: SQLite graph library for a self-evolving repository (recollection)
members.problem: The owner remembered a graph-based library with faster, token-minimal recall that improves itself; the question was where it lives and whether it works.
members.mechanism: Not built in the clinic lane: no SQLite file, graph or self-modifying part exists. Nearest pieces: exact-text recall, agent-maintained notes, a JSONL map, and outside tools using SQLite and summary DAGs.
members.status_note: Idea only in this lane; the knowledge-store track (PR #183) is the place it would come from.
members.results: Not yet tested; no graph or SQLite recall measured. Nothing in the line learns or rewrites anything automatically.

members.name: Abstaining retrieval: miss, candidate or lead
members.problem: At a few hundred entries a wrong hit acted on is the dangerous failure and a miss is cheap; raw search scores cannot serve as confidence, and a repair-time lookup must never leak customer data into the store.
members.mechanism: Canonicalise and scrub (phones, CNIC, placeholders), exact-handle prefilter, three-table BM25 ranking, then abstain on score-free features (exact hit, IDF-weighted coverage, margin). Output is miss, candidate or lead, max one of each, inside a 2,000-character cap; a write gate refuses duplicates and self-matches.
members.status_note: Sections 4.1-4.2; thresholds proposed in KS-2, frozen in KS-4. Sonnet implements, Opus reviews the scrubber as a security boundary. Customer-name case recorded as a known scrubber miss.
members.results: Not yet tested. Starting values theta_lead 0.5, theta_cand 0.3, margin 0.2 (S, owner parameters).
members.aka: lookup pipeline, abstention, three-valued output, KS-2, write gate, recipe v1

members.name: Exactly-once proof and planted-fault demos
members.problem: A faster or stricter gate must not be weaker: a split must never drop a test or print PASS wrongly, a passing test does not prove its guard works, and environment variables can steer a gate.
members.mechanism: Judge the split by test ids (parallel ids equal serial's left-out ids, disjoint); skipped/xfailed/xpassed fail; environment scrubbed. Planted faults and guard removals must make the check fail; each ticked box records its command and a negative run.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic gate (model-reviewed, no human reviewer); the per-tick negative-run line is a trial for FixFlow in P1 and the next two code phases.
members.results: Baseline 1,953 ids vs 1,972 (1,844 parallel + 128 serial, none in both) (M). Six planted faults gave CHECK FAILED 5/7 (collected 2526, failed 2, errors 2, skipped 1, xfailed 1) (M); S00 clean: 7/7, 220 tests, 0 skipped (M). Round 6 found a session P1 (mypy not run).
members.aka: A3-12, A8-10, A2-06, G4-F152, lock-removal experiments, nothing-weaker proof

members.name: Close findings only on executed tests with positive controls
members.problem: Findings and claims close on a model's say-so; verification tooling itself reported success wrongly (a drill printed PASS while testing nothing; race tests passed without the lock they claimed to prove).
members.mechanism: A finding closes only on a harness-run test with a positive control: every 'nothing found' check needs a case it must find; drills must fail on empty inputs; remove one lock at a time and show the named test fails, recording the failing assertion.
members.status_note: Lock-removal experiments and positive-control rules in use in the testbed (at least four instances later found to prove less than claimed); the compile proposes it as a trial in the root's gate.
members.results: S05 race evidence '71 against 73 without them' (M). Cutoff guards RS-2 and RS-5 failed with guard removed; removing GD-05's check left every test passing (M). S11 round 1: 1 P1, 15 P2, 18 P3 (M).
members.aka: executed acceptance, positive control, lock-removal experiments, A2-06, A4-07

members.name: Red-team of the workflow gates and repair plan
members.problem: The workflow's own gates could pass while checking nothing; the gates needed testing.
members.mechanism: A 3 Oct nine-perspective review found nine defects (RT-01 to RT-09), each with reproduction and closure condition; a 5 Oct plan orders repairs with real dependencies and one integrating implementer each.
members.status_note: Source marks it abandoned: no code repair was made, the build moved to application slices.
members.results: 3 P1, 5 P2, 1 P3; eight OPEN (M). All-skipped suite passes with exit 0 (29 skipped); faulty artifact exits 2 normally and 0 under python -O (M). 262 files covered.

members.name: One fact, one command
members.problem: An unchecked agent report once produced a false harness rule (that subagents cannot write), and first-deploy steps can be ticked without proof; five facts in the original bottleneck list turned out wrong.
members.mechanism: A fact or rule is checked by one command before it becomes a rule, recorded 'verified' or 'contradicted'. Each first-deploy step carries its command, expected result and a negative run, such as a planted failure.
members.status_note: Compile calls it trial, v2 design adopts it from phase 1; costs a brief line.
members.results: Not yet tested. Baseline count planned: environment facts in the root's 15 [M] lessons that one command could check, and the 21 statements one command could check.
members.aka: Command-backed facts and checklist steps, G2-F180, G4-F152, Mechanism 7

members.name: Transcript tally at phase close
members.problem: Routine steps that leave no git or GitHub trace (Fable never edits code, SHA in reviewer brief, cold-resume dispatch) look the same whether done or skipped.
members.mechanism: A read-only zero-dependency Node script over the session JSONL (main plus subagents) scores a fixed list of routine steps from tool_use records and compares with the closing message. External mirror, event-log replay and the 'store consulted' criterion were refuted.
members.status_note: Top trial 2 in §0; about 100 lines (E); must run within 7 days before transcripts are pruned.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Transcript audit at each merge
members.problem: The merge record is self-reported and fields have been filled falsely; no independent source says whether a reviewer read the final head or how many edits the root made.
members.mechanism: A read-only script over the harness's own tool-call transcripts and raw event logs: did a reviewer read the final head, did the gate run before each fix commit, how many root edits touched shared files. Records only, blocks nothing.
members.status_note: The zero-model-call audit was used once in the clinic testbed; the merge-time version is designed for v2 phase 3, no tokens. Depends on transcripts surviving cleanup (retention unverified).
members.results: Clinic audit: 0 model calls, complete cohort verified, context_gain_proven false (M). Merge version not yet run; must find the 10 and 11 Nov unread heads by itself.

members.name: Phase-scoped skill trigger tally
members.problem: Skills may never load in the phases their descriptions name, and nothing shows it.
members.mechanism: At each phase close, grep the session transcript (main plus subagent files and workflow scripts) for Skill calls and agents that preload a skill; tabulate against the phases each description names. A cap and pruning were refuted.
members.status_note: To run over the first six phase sessions.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: One-off owner watch of P1
members.problem: Live watching might catch costly departures earlier than a transcript audit afterward.
members.mechanism: The owner watches P1 through its first code commit and writes each departure into the owner-corrections journal without interrupting the cold-resume subagent. A fresh agent then audits the transcript against a fixed section-0 list.
members.status_note: P1 only; kept only if it catches something the audit would find late.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Diff lookup: warn from the PR's real diff
members.problem: Error-text lookups cannot reach silent hazards, such as a forbidden change that removes login throttling; a missed warning there permanently costs.
members.mechanism: At first commit, PR-ready, the Opus review and ks close, run git diff -U0 between base and head; match author-named identifiers on changed lines, config values and protective-test blobs against do-not-apply, open-defect and trap entries. One warning line per entry, inside an output cap.
members.status_note: Built in KS-2 and KS-3; judged in the pilot's diff arm; no hook needed.
members.results: Replay on 154 first-parent commits: v1.3 rule would warn on 48.7 percent (M); 27 to 44 percent with strict handles (M); ex4 warned on 13 commits where a file join fired on 47 (M). Costs 170 to 220 ms a run (M).
members.aka: ks lookup --diff, KS-O10, KS-P1..P10, do-not-apply warning

members.name: Diff lookup warnings quoted by the reviewer
members.problem: A forbidden change (a refuted fix, an open defect) never raises an error, so error-triggered lookup cannot stop it; a reviewer sentence 'ran the check' could be satisfied vacuously.
members.mechanism: At first commit, PR-ready, in the Opus review and inside ks close, the CLI matches identifiers on changed lines against author-named handles and protected files and prints one warning per matched entry. The reviewer runs it at the PR head SHA, quotes its first line and answers each warning; exit 3, 4, 5 or missing CLI reads 'diff check not run'.
members.status_note: Declarative part in KS-3; a go criterion at the pilot (D8); reviewer wiring in KS-7 as a plan amendment after a pilot go.
members.results: Not yet tested; offline replay against git history planned. On history, ex4's handles would have warned on 13 of 154 past commits (M), against 47 for a file-level join (M).
members.aka: ks lookup --diff, KS-O10, KS-O11, KS-P9, recall-first diff check

members.name: Knowledge-store lookup and record steps in the phase routine
members.problem: Lookup, diff check and recording only happen if the phase procedure names them and reviewers verify them; escalating a tier without a lookup pays the top tier for a repeat.
members.mechanism: About 260 words added to ship plan section 0 after the pilot says go: ks lookup before escalating or retrying, diff lookups at first commit and PR-ready, ks record before PR-ready, ks close at phase end; reviewer quotes the diff lookup's first line.
members.status_note: Proposed text only, not applied by PR #183; conditional on a pilot go or go-minimal. Store never blocks a ship phase. Compliance self-reported, no hook.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: Step-zero lookup before escalating a tier, section 7.6 plan text, Wire-in: plan hook, prospective log, CLAUDE.md trim, KS-7, D10

members.name: Net-zero CLAUDE.md edit, then trim to rules plus ids
members.problem: CLAUDE.md is loaded by every agent every session and must stay honest, yet the knowledge store adds a runtime that CLAUDE.md's own rule says to document.
members.mechanism: KS-1 rewrites the CI row in place (no new line). After the pilot, KS-7 keeps each invariant's rule sentence plus a store id, moves diagnostic paragraphs into verified entries, shrinks the four build traps to one line each; MEMORY.md gains one pointer line.
members.status_note: Trim only after a pilot go, one verified entry at a time.
members.results: Not yet tested. Line counts before and after are recorded in the KS-7 PR body.

members.name: Gates in their own phase, long agents first
members.problem: Test and build gates run 25 to 40 minutes and must not block or collide with the reader agents.
members.mechanism: S-07a, S-07b and S-08 issue first in a separate Gates phase and are not awaited by reader slices; their write set (node_modules, dist, coverage, Docker) is disjoint from what readers read.
members.status_note: Part of the W1 contract.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Staged workflows with judging gates between them
members.problem: A large investigation needs cheap wide discovery, narrow expensive deep dives and a recorded decision between stages, so the plan is designed only after a verified picture exists, without a synthesis agent adding a layer.
members.mechanism: W0 owner pre-flight, W1 cheap discovery, G1 gate, W2 Opus deep-dive, G2 gate, then S3 phase plan. Gates are the main session reading results by id and writing a record with verdicts, conflicts adjudicated and decisions; zero agents at gates.
members.status_note: Run for the ship program: G1 and G2 written 2026-11-01; Stage 3 phased plan followed (S3 itself was designed after G2).
members.results: W1: 16/16 coverage, about 1.67M subagent tokens, 14 min [M]. W2: 8 analysts, 139 findings, about 3.3M tokens, 23 min [M].
members.aka: W0/W1/G1/W2/G2/S3, fixflow-discover and fixflow-deep-dive workflows, wide-cheap then narrow-expensive, G1 and G2 reading by id, gate records

members.name: Owner-decision form issued at a gate
members.problem: Design agents (Odoo, self-host) cannot be right without owner answers, and spending Opus before those answers is spending on a guess. Owner decisions also block phases.
members.mechanism: At gate G1 a numbered decision form is issued per design task (Odoo and self-host question lists). The owner's answers become parameters, not assumptions. W2 may start without answers, but tasks O-07 and O-08 may not. If answers narrow scope, scope narrows but tier does not drop, since money invariants hold whatever the transport.
members.status_note: Designed in the orchestration document, then issued at G1; the owner's answers are still pending in the record.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: Owner-decision form, Odoo and self-host question lists

members.name: W0 owner pre-flight before any agent spends tokens
members.problem: Agents cannot learn facts only the owner can see (dashboards, devices, billing), and spending tokens on guesses wastes money.
members.mechanism: A roughly 30 minute owner checklist runs first: fleet notice, hostname control, APK signing, Supabase/R2/Railway/Sentry/EAS status, workshop coordinates, Docker started. Outputs decide the G1 branch and feed later agents.
members.status_note: The design waits on W0 before W1; later carried into FixFlow's P0a pre-flight kit.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Map store with bounded chunk readers
members.problem: Extract relations from a big document set without one agent reading everything, and without long reports passing through the orchestrator.
members.mechanism: Chunk by heading (at most 6,000 characters); one fresh reader per chunk writes a file; a script validates; one sequential writer ingests into JSON-lines files; resume from pending-chunk state, not conversation memory.
members.status_note: Built; only synthetic tests; construction cost never recorded.
members.results: 51 chunks over 11 files read and ingested [M]; 3,361 attested records, 2,201,401 bytes for a 167,342-byte corpus [M]; 11 synthetic tests pass [M]; tokens and time not measured.

members.name: Corpus map of typed edges for the planning documents
members.problem: Planning documents are hard to navigate and recall relies on reading; fresh agents need bounded, source-cited context from the plan with known gaps, not whole documents or a prose summary.
members.mechanism: A versioned map of 11 planning files as JSON-line typed edges with exact line spans, one status per record (attested, codebook, overlay, reconstructed, candidate, derived), a coverage ledger and hash-based refresh; packets computed from base records each call.
members.status_note: Design (99 rules) plus an operational prototype on 11 files; never used by a coding agent. One source marks it abandoned at P9-4, trials not started; validation contract frozen and never run; adoption is a pending owner decision.
members.results: 3,361 records for a 167 KB corpus; extraction recall 0.52 against an earlier reading (M). 99 rules: 55 borrowed, 44 required (M); rejection check 401 cells, 197 pass, 192 N/A, 12 fail (M); skeptic 21 attacks, 12 accepted. Pilot did not reproduce an independent annotator's chain. No token or time measurement.
members.aka: A6-01 to A6-13, A6-01, A6-03, A8-13, corpus map with status model S1-S6, corpus map of the plan

members.name: Frozen validation contract for any map or store
members.problem: Maps and stores were built without testing whether they help over existing routed reading.
members.mechanism: Pre-registered and sealed: 5 cases, 3 arms (map, routed reading, Graphify), 2 runs each = 30 runs, 16,000 tokens and 30 calls per run, blinded scoring, 'better' needs a 0.10 mean gap in 4 of 5 cases; fewer tokens with a missing prerequisite is not a win.
members.status_note: Frozen and never run; the clinic work moved to context-admission research.
members.results: Not yet tested; the runs folder is empty.
members.aka: A6-10, map vs routed reading vs Graphify

members.name: Pilot of the attested-only map on four files
members.problem: Check whether the map recovers the dependency chain a human annotator saw.
members.mechanism: Four frozen files read under the design by a skeptic and an independent annotator; counts C1-C7, then re-application under the revised design and an L3 check.
members.status_note: Informative: shows what the strict design cannot express.
members.results: v1: 427 attested edges, chain not reproduced at any level (M); v2: 692 attested edges, 242 labels (148 used once), 1,166 dangling endpoints at L2 (M). Links through a shared value such as '$8' cannot be joined.

members.name: Clinic context system (snapshot, restore, recall)
members.problem: Keep context across compaction and sessions: snapshot before compaction, restore at session start, recall past facts, admit large reads selectively, and do it without a database.
members.mechanism: Hooks snapshot at PreCompact and restore at SessionStart, restoring only declared task-state whole blocks or nothing. Snapshots are immutable checksummed files, the meta file written last; recall is a linear scan. Python, built in the clinic repository.
members.status_note: Built in the clinic repo and verified offline on synthetic cases and copies of two real transcripts; never run in a live session. Owner decision 2026-11-01: stays in its own repository; skipped for FixFlow. Continuation quality after restore on Claude not tested.
members.results: 85 offline tests (M); defects reproduced then fixed: 6 + 15 + 22 + 10 across review waves (M). Scan of 115 MB in about 1 s (M); storage stress at 1, 4, 8 and 16 processes gave 464 events and 464 snapshots, exact (M). Ruled out keyword heading matching, time-based expiry, project-wide focus pointer.
members.aka: context system, large-read admission, A5-05, A5-02, declared-state restoration contract, plain-file snapshot storage

members.name: Context system: compaction steering and exact recall
members.problem: Long sessions swell past 700k tokens and are summarised at a bad moment, losing decisions and next steps. Aim: 300-400k active tokens carrying the quality of an ~800k history.
members.mechanism: Standard-library Python hooks: lower the compaction trigger to 400000, snapshot declared task-state sections before compaction, restore them verbatim after, archive the summary, nudge ~40k tokens early, exact-text recall over transcripts with no model calls, large-read gate.
members.status_note: Built and checked offline; never installed in the clinic project, never run live. AGENTS.md says it moves to its own repository.
members.results: 85 regression tests pass (M); repro script 35/35 (M); hook run 0.1-0.2 s on real transcripts (M); recall over 211 transcripts (115.3 MB) 0.52-1.06 s (M); 53 hook defects over four review rounds (M). Quality at 300-400k vs full history and pause length: not yet measured.
members.aka: tools/context_system, A5-01 to A5-07, A8-12, Compaction-steering hook package

members.name: Exact-text recall with stable path:line references
members.problem: After a reset an agent re-reads or re-derives what earlier sessions already said, or cannot verify what a session really said.
members.mechanism: ctx.py recall scans transcripts, subagent transcripts and the archive for terms (no model calls), ranks by distinct terms then recency, and 'show' reopens the exact record by a path:line:block reference.
members.status_note: Built; no live evidence it saves tokens.
members.results: 1 s over 211 transcripts / 115 MB (M); token saving not yet measured; in the 2026-10-14 screen no arm used journal recall (M).

members.name: Context-system line moves to its own repository
members.problem: Experimental memory tooling should stay off the product's routes and out of its history; the line currently sits untracked in a repository with no remote.
members.mechanism: Owner decision of 1 November 2026: the line continues in its own repository at low priority. Until moved it stays untracked, and measurement research does not start unless asked.
members.status_note: Parked; the move needs the owner's folder name and has not happened.
members.results: Not applicable (decision).

members.name: Context-file and skill-description shaping
members.problem: FixFlow's CLAUDE.md and 24k characters of skill and agent descriptions may load more than needed or contradict each other, costing context and obedience.
members.mechanism: Wrap conditional CLAUDE.md blocks with narrow triggers; split single-runtime rules into directory-scoped files; trim skill descriptions with a routing check; one sweep for contradictions; side-by-side model-change regression of invariant adherence.
members.status_note: All trial and FixFlow-only. The testbed's context-machinery trials found no gain, and no bottleneck is about the instructions file being missed.
members.results: Not yet tested; testbed context trials were null.

members.name: Trim skill and agent descriptions to 400 characters
members.problem: About 24k characters of skill and agent descriptions load into context for every session.
members.mechanism: Trim each of the 13 skill and 11 agent descriptions to at most 400 characters (key use case first, one 'do not' clause). The disable-flag half was refuted because it blocks subagent preload.
members.status_note: An L2 gain only; needs a routing check before adoption.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Wrap conditional CLAUDE.md rules in 'important if'
members.problem: Long CLAUDE.md files get skimmed; rules that only matter for certain tasks dilute the always-true ones.
members.mechanism: Authoring rule for the wrapped arm of the CLAUDE.md adherence trial (E1): conditional rules wrapped in <important if> tags, always-true content bare; adds 3 oblique probes whose task text does not name the trigger.
members.status_note: Only as one arm of E1; the technique alone fell to the knowledge-store ruling that keeps every rule.
members.results: Not yet tested; his adherence claims carry no measurements.

members.name: Split CLAUDE.md by runtime (nested files)
members.problem: CLAUDE.md is 390 lines, about twice the length where adherence is known to fall; every task pays for backend and mobile detail it may not need.
members.mechanism: Move one-runtime material to backend/CLAUDE.md and technician-app/CLAUDE.md; keep every cross-runtime rule and a pointer index in the root. Test briefs and diff-only reviewers too, since nested files load only on a Read.
members.status_note: A 'split' arm of E1 on a branch; refuter confirmed nested files attach on Read here.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Resume mismatch guard: stop when record and branch disagree
members.problem: After many power-offs a session's task record and its branch can drift apart. A released session may start fresh over commits its record does not cover, duplicating or discarding work.
members.mechanism: On release or resume, if the record is missing, lacks the Plan @ sha line, the sha is unreachable, or the branch holds commits the record does not cover, list them and stop and ask. A matching record resumes with no wait. G2-F056 adds a git fetch first.
members.status_note: Adopted in PR #186 for FixFlow (helps W3 only); designed into harness v2 from phase 1. For the testbed it may stay dormant if the replay finds no mismatch. Nothing in the lists restarts Docker or a session after a power-off.
members.results: Not yet tested. Proof planned: replay the 9 November mass resume and count sessions whose record disagreed with their branch head; zero means unproven and the guard stays dormant. A fault-injected dispatch (branch with one commit, no PR) is planned in the P1 cold-resume trial.
members.aka: G2-F054, G2-F056, mechanism 8, Resume check, Missing resume source stops and asks

members.name: Plan @ sha in the PR body, with resume fetch and diff
members.problem: A session that restarts or compacts does not know which plan version it worked from, and may miss an amendment because git only updates origin/main on a fetch.
members.mechanism: The draft PR body starts with 'Plan @ <sha>'. On resume run git fetch origin, then git diff --stat from that sha to origin/main for docs/program/ and re-read only changed sections; each journal records the sha read after the fetch.
members.status_note: Reviewer ruling adopt; lands in plan section 0 Resume; the fetch line is adopt, narrowed to one-line form.
members.results: Not yet tested. Pass test: each recorded sha equals git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main at that moment, P0a to P5.
members.aka: plan-sha resume rule, HR-C2 (part), G2-F056, git fetch before the resume check

members.name: Advisory CI check on PR bodies
members.problem: Whether the phase routine ran is self-reported; the PR body's Plan @ sha line, journal heading and reviewer verdict naming the head SHA can be missing with no alarm.
members.mechanism: A separate dependency-free GitHub Actions workflow on PR events asserts line 1 matches 'Plan @ <sha>' and resolves, a task-list item exists, the journal heading exists and the reviewer verdict names the head SHA. Advisory on drafts, fails when ready.
members.status_note: Top trial 3 in the Horthy sweep; about 40 lines of YAML [E]; natural home phase P1-ci; trial over the first 5 code-phase PRs.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: One run per lane lock and fixed container names
members.problem: Two gate runs against one database deadlock or drop each other's database, a cleanup trap could remove another run's containers, and re-issuing a mutating command after a timeout can duplicate effects.
members.mechanism: A directory lock named for lane and kind is taken first; a second run is refused with exit 4. Fixed container names make a second start fail on a name conflict. Timeout 600000 ms, never re-issue a mutating command, clean up at the end.
members.status_note: Lock proved by a refused second run (exit 4); the lock is reclaimed if older than the last boot or its process is gone. Container-name rule designed, to be verified with a forced second start.
members.results: Second run refused with exit 4 (M).
members.aka: per-lane lock, ALREADY_RUNNING exit 4, no second pytest on one DB

members.name: Docker engine up first; agents never start it
members.problem: Backend gates run only in Docker, and an agent that starts or reconfigures Docker could damage the machine.
members.mechanism: The owner starts Docker Desktop before W1; the first command of any Docker agent is docker info; on failure the agent returns blocked DOCKER_ENGINE_DOWN and does nothing else.
members.status_note: The Docker engine was down when the design was written.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Shared-machine etiquette and session ceiling
members.problem: Another project's containers run on the same PC, so touching Docker could break them, and too many sessions exhaust RAM.
members.mechanism: A FixFlow session removes only containers named fixflow-*, never restarts Docker or WSL, never prunes networks, and replaces shared scripts by atomic rename. Eight sessions is the ceiling, near six when RAM is tight, until some finish.
members.status_note: Rated adopt and in force.
members.results: With eight lane sessions: 5.5 to 7.7 GB free of 31, commit 35 to 41.5 of 50.1 GB (M).

members.name: Checks must be able to fail (RT lessons)
members.problem: Gates go green without testing anything: accepted rows beside failed checks, bare asserts, boot tests run in a dirty environment, unknown recorded as zero.
members.mechanism: Carry the clinic red-team lessons as plan rules, no machinery: no accepted row beside a failed AFTER check (RT-03); decisive checks use if/raise not assert (RT-02); boot test in a cleaned environment (RT-05); unknown recorded as unknown, never 0 (RT-06).
members.status_note: Carried as plan rules; the BAML sweep confirmed the harness already holds them.
members.results: Confirmed as already done (BAML sweep); not otherwise tested.
members.aka: RT-01..RT-06 lessons, T-03, Never mark verification done when the check proved nothing

members.name: Record unknown as unknown, never zero
members.problem: Treating missing data as 0 makes a gap look like a measured absence.
members.mechanism: Store unmeasured values as 'unknown' and write decisive checks with if/raise, never bare assert.
members.status_note: Stated lesson.
members.results: Not separately measured.

members.name: Escape-hatch values in every schema
members.problem: A forced schema can make a model invent a conforming answer when the input does not fit.
members.mechanism: Schemas carry UNVERIFIABLE, untestable, UNCLEAR, unknown, NONE, exit_code -1, or empty values; unknown is recorded as unknown.
members.status_note: Already done; a one-pass audit for required fields lacking an unknown path is suggested.
members.results: Agents wrote 'undated' honestly in this run.

members.name: Stop hook that re-runs the CI checks
members.problem: An agent can finish with a red tree.
members.mechanism: A Stop hook runs the same quality and typecheck commands as CI and exits 2 with only the errors; hook scripts are thin aliases onto human-run commands.
members.status_note: First pass left it deferred (over the cap, no refuter verdict); addendum rules skip: reopens the pre-commit-hook skip, backend gates run in Docker for minutes, Fable never implements. Hooks are a skipped area.
members.results: not yet tested; no verdict

members.name: Hooks (stop hook, tool-event heartbeat)
members.problem: Claims and progress are not enforced automatically: nothing blocks a session on a failed claim check or shows progress from tool events.
members.mechanism: Settings-based Claude Code hooks: a stop hook blocks on a failed claim check; a heartbeat is fed by tool events.
members.status_note: Stay off in harness v2; the owner may re-open for two uses (D17). Root-gate versions need no hook.
members.results: Built or designed in the testbed, no gain shown.

members.name: Edit-time warning hook
members.problem: A forbidden edit should warn at edit time, not only in review.
members.mechanism: A fail-open PreToolUse or PostToolUse hook on Edit and Write runs git diff -U0 on the edited path through the same join; one warning of up to 300 characters, deduped, never blocking.
members.status_note: Default off; blind to Bash and PowerShell edits; ruled at KS-9 if the warning rate is within the ceiling.
members.results: not yet tested.

members.name: Tests that assert documents match the code
members.problem: Shared documents go stale against the code.
members.mechanism: Tests parse registry documents and routing/context documents and fail when they differ from the plan or code.
members.status_note: In use for registry-like tables only; AGENTS.md and the context map have none.
members.results: Drift caught was not counted. Root document edits broke three tests at gates.

members.name: CI check that CLAUDE.md facts match the code
members.problem: The agent instruction file drifts from the code (for example the migration head number), and agents then trust the wrong fact.
members.mechanism: CI fails if CLAUDE.md's Alembic head differs from the end of the down_revision chain; a second check warns when paths named in CLAUDE.md no longer resolve, with an allow-list.
members.status_note: P1 deliverable; the path check is a warning until P13c.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Dated audits by parallel automated reviewers
members.problem: Find stale guidance and missing evidence in a repo before building on it; a self-built recall tool still lacked a boundary on what enters context.
members.mechanism: Three parallel automated reviewers (planning, research, workflow) plus an integration review over 61 files, separating hash-verified preservation from substantive review; a static local-fit audit reads a tool's code against its admission requirement, plus a subagent peer review.
members.status_note: Done once; automated, not human review; static observations, not reproduced defects.
members.results: 61 files reviewed (M); 14 findings RC-01..RC-14 (M); 641 cached members re-hashed with no failures (M); 5 peer-review corrections PR-01..PR-05 closed by 2026-10-09 (M). Cost not recorded.
members.aka: A6-23, A6-21, peer review of own tools

members.name: Dependency-cruiser import rules for mobile
members.problem: Mobile has no boundary enforcement, so the invariant 'never fetch a write outside the outbox' is only prose.
members.mechanism: dependency-cruiser in technician-app with rules mirroring the backend import-linter: screens and components may not import write functions of lib/*Api; raw fetch confined to lib/api.ts and lib/outboxSync.ts; run in CI beside the mobile job.
members.status_note: Adopted as the better alternative to graphify; phase P5b-2.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Architecture rules file plus CI boundary checks
members.problem: Agents drift from architecture without durable rules and enforced boundaries.
members.mechanism: CLAUDE.md invariants plus import-linter and ESLint boundary checks in CI.
members.status_note: Already done.
members.results: Confirmed.

members.name: Existing code maps: import contracts, CODE-MAP, Haiku locator
members.problem: Agents need to find where a feature lives without a call-graph tool.
members.mechanism: Import-boundary contracts (import-linter on the backend, ESLint on the web), a hand-written docs/CODE-MAP.md and a Haiku locator agent.
members.status_note: Existing; mobile has no boundary enforcement yet.
members.results: not measured

members.name: Stop after 3 identical CI failures
members.problem: An agent can keep pushing and rerunning until CI turns green, masking a real failure.
members.mechanism: One line in the Gates section: if the same CI job fails on 3 consecutive pushes after local gates are green, stop, record it in the journal and hand it to the owner; never rerun to green without journaling; keep PR Auto-fix off.
members.status_note: Flaky-rerun allowance dropped.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Flow limits for loops and work in progress
members.problem: Automated loops can flood review with parallel PRs, overrun review capacity, or touch unsafe areas.
members.mechanism: Bound work in progress to one open PR per loop, restrict the actuator to safe directories with batch caps, and widen frequency or batch only after output has been reviewed clean.
members.status_note: One listing was deferred over the cap with no refuter verdict (reviewers split trial vs already-done); the later assessment says WIP bounds already exist in section 0 and ORCHESTRATION, and there are no scheduled agent loops here.
members.results: not yet tested; no verdict
members.aka: G4-F210, Control-loop flow limits for automation

members.name: Governor: slow lanes so the token window lasts
members.problem: At the five-hour window's limit every lane stops at once; 14 limit episodes in October.
members.mechanism: Keep governor share = what the window can still carry divided by what lanes would burn, using measured tokens per lane-hour by model, so lanes slow instead of everything stopping.
members.status_note: Built in phase 5 after the baseline; depends on measured rates.
members.results: Not yet tested. One window covered about 3.4 million subagent tokens (M); subagents caused 91 of 104 limit errors (M).
members.aka: B3 Limit stop control, Token budget governor

members.name: Record-only deterministic checks over returned objects
members.problem: Agent outputs are checked by judges or by eye; cheap rule checks (quote length, unique ids, URLs listed) could catch violations the gates missed, without spending tokens.
members.mechanism: A node script over docs/program/evidence/**/*.json checks: quote at most 15 words, each could_not_read URL present in urls_attempted, unique ids, evidence in path:line - quote form with an allow-list. Run record-only, no retry.
members.status_note: One of four surviving trials; the refuter downgraded it from adopt.
members.results: Not yet tested. The refuter's naive regex flagged 174 of 707 W2 evidence strings (M), mostly legitimate, so the allow-list is the work.

members.name: Claims file and verdict script per gate round
members.problem: Session reports overstate what was run: reports cite tests or evidence that do not exist or do not match (20-plus recorded overstatements, M). A model re-reading its own claims has not caught this.
members.mechanism: Each slice commits a claims file; a script checks each cited test exists, ran, and fails when its guard is removed. Per fixed finding it runs the test at the fix's parent and at head, counts assertion failures against collection errors, and compares base and head tests for weakened expectations.
