members.status_note: Machine check was never built in the clinic repo; designed into v2, replay over recorded gates first, side by side with the root's reading for a wave. A3-14 flaky tests can fail a base rerun wrongly, so a rerun rule is needed.
members.results: Not yet run. At least 20 overstatement records counted by reading, no denominator (M). Target false flags under 10 % (T).
members.aka: Mechanism 2, claims-versus-evidence check, G4-F086, G1-F085, G2-F015, G4-F073, T-08, G2-F114, fail-on-base pass-on-head script

members.name: FixFlow facts first, cited to path and line
members.problem: Generic outside advice wastes tokens and can mislead agents on this repo; stale line numbers and vague dates make claims uncheckable.
members.mechanism: Generic sections shrink to a rule and reason; words go to repo specifics (file, constant, phase, register id). Every claim is cited path:line, verified at write time; web facts carry URL and fetch date; dates absolute; versions exact.
members.status_note: Rule set applied across PR #185 packages; facts re-read on 2026-11-04.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Do-not-apply entries with proposed-change check
members.problem: A rule such as 'a locked account must refuse even a correct PIN' needs a check that fires before the forbidden change lands, not after.
members.mechanism: ks verify --target proposed runs a four-outcome rule: applies (protective test fails), stop(protection_changed), stop(protection_disabled), inconclusive(coverage_unknown). The fix text (the prohibition) is never withheld.
members.status_note: Declarative half in KS-3 (no Docker); executable half in KS-6b.
members.results: not yet tested. 3 of 3 past edits to the protective files were legitimate (M), so stops go to the reviewer.

members.name: Entries with diagnosis path, negative results, do-not-apply
members.problem: What failed and why is the costly part to save and a strong agent may retry it; some prescribed fixes are wrong; a note that 'X failed' goes stale silently after an upgrade or blocks a fix that now works.
members.mechanism: Each entry holds symptom-first title, cause, conditions, ordered diagnosis steps, fix, failed approaches with proof level, validity predicate; kinds include do_not_apply and open_defect. A negative result enters only with the footprint it was seen on, found by action words or exact error text.
members.status_note: Schema in section 3.2; fix text withheld until an applies gate run exists, except do-not-apply prohibitions. Not built.
members.results: Not yet tested. Eight worked examples reconstructed from git history show which are lead-capable today. Walked savings mostly estimated: 'enable dispatcher' would reach the hazard behind 36 [G] messages about old jobs; the stranded-fix scan fits June and would remove 16 [G] days of broken main.
members.aka: entry model, negative results first-class, do_not_apply entries, KS-R2, stranded-fix scan, exact error text lookup

members.name: Eight handle kinds with canonicalised error templates
members.problem: The same root cause shows up with different error text, files and words, so one key per entry would miss or mis-merge symptoms.
members.mechanism: Each entry carries several key types: canonical error template, tool+phase signature, top in-app frames, command context, prose paraphrases, author-named identifiers, doc pointers, action intents. A mask pipeline scrubs ids and numbers; each key keeps its recipe version and raw text.
members.status_note: Section 3.3; recipe is code with golden fixtures built from the repo's own traps.
members.results: Not yet tested. Selectivity check example: ex6's diff yields 113 tokens firing on 91% of commits (M), so handles are author-named, not derived.

members.name: Device evidence across OEMs before reliability claims
members.problem: One phone can discriminate between hypotheses but cannot validate a fix across the phone brands (OEMs) in the fleet.
members.mechanism: Any geofencing reliability claim requires device evidence across the OEMs in the fleet; a discriminating field protocol using adb separates the top hypotheses.
members.status_note: Constraint on the phased plan.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Code yields candidates, device evidence yields conclusions
members.problem: Reading code on the main branch cannot say what an older build on real phones does, so confident code audits can mislead.
members.mechanism: Every finding is labelled in_field_apk (yes/no/unknown) and a field protocol, not the audit, decides what the phones do today. Findings from main are treated as candidates.
members.status_note: Became a rule in v3.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: android-field-debugging skill and device debugger agent
members.problem: Truth about geofencing and offline queues lives on phones, and the field APK is older than main, so code reading gives only candidates.
members.mechanism: A sourced skill for read-only adb, dumpsys and logcat evidence capture and the geofence evidence chain; a Sonnet agent returns a DEVICE-EVIDENCE table. It never installs, clears, force-stops or judges reliability.
members.status_note: Skill and agent on draft PR #185, not merged.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Design adjudicated by sweep, judge panel, refuters and owner critique
members.problem: A design from one session carries unchecked claims; one architect's design is one guess; an owner critique is sometimes right and sometimes misjudged, so neither obeying nor ignoring it is safe.
members.mechanism: Four workflows: 57-agent research sweep, four Opus architects scored by three Opus judges, 31 refuters plus a completeness critic, then each owner-critique point to two Opus verifiers with Sonnet checkers and a synthesiser. Raw outputs kept with sha256 manifest.
members.status_note: Applied to the knowledge-store design; judges were lost once to a usage limit and re-run from cached proposals; narrowed three owner-critique mechanisms, changed no component.
members.results: About 15M subagent tokens [M] across first three workflows. Scores out of 360: A 292, C 282, D 281, B 222 [M]. Owner critique verdicts: partly right x3, mostly right x1 [M]; 17 agents; 20 amendments.
members.aka: §12.7, KS-O1..O20, KS-P refuter pass, KS-A1..A6, critique 2026-11-03, wf_2bb8c274-f02, wf_926f16a5-8dc, wf_4c53797c-5fb, wf_2c872948-51a

members.name: Completeness critic over a draft
members.problem: Drafts miss mechanisms without phases, contradictions and owner-readability.
members.mechanism: One Opus xhigh critic reads the draft plus register and lists missing items, unsupported statements, contradictions and readability problems; every item is folded in as a numbered amendment.
members.status_note: Run twice on the knowledge-store design.
members.results: 19 missing, 15 unsupported, 19 contradictions, 9 readability items (M); later 22 contradictions, 15 mismatches, 17 leftovers (M).

members.name: Multi-lens panel with judges and refuters before work
members.problem: A plan repaired in place can hide a wrong foundation; the owner wanted the architecture reviewed, with every recommendation tested rather than argued, before work started. A design written alone carries blind spots.
members.mechanism: Four Opus architects propose, one lens each; two Opus judges (one skeptical of change, one of keeping) score each area 0-10 per lens; 45 falsifiable claims each get two Opus refuters; the main session rules and labels rulings HR-. Earlier designs got three Opus critics and two external reviews.
members.status_note: Orchestration design critiqued in two rounds; architecture panel run once on 2026-11-01, rulings HR-A1a..HR-A4 bound the plan from v6. Overhead-skeptic dissent on the owner view was recorded and overruled.
members.results: 101 agents (94 completed, 7 refuters lost to a usage limit), about 10.1M subagent tokens, 34 minutes (M). Verdict: no wrong foundation; plan moved to v6. Adopt/skip table: 11 rows adopted or trialled once, 8 skipped (M).
members.aka: wf_07e89689-064, adoption-maximalist vs overhead-skeptic, three Opus critics, external reviews, opposed-stance reviewer pairs

members.name: Transcript-derived read audit of analysts
members.problem: Analyst reading rules are brief text and extra reads are self-reported and unenforced, so nobody can tell whether an analyst obeyed them.
members.mechanism: A short node script compares an analyst's self-listed extra reads with the Read/Grep calls in its subagent transcript (agent-<id>.jsonl).
members.status_note: Trial, unrefuted. Feasibility settled: a lane reader's transcript holds 115 tool_use entries.
members.results: Feasibility only: transcripts do record tool calls (M). Mismatch rate not yet measured.

members.name: Reading rules: grep first, then ranged reads
members.problem: Agents read whole large files and cite facts they never saw; spend is invisible and evidence second-hand.
members.mechanism: Never read a file over 300 lines whole: Grep the symbol, then Read a range. Follow imports one hop and list extra files read; map facts cited for context only; the explorer reads at most 40 lines. No npm, docker or git.
members.status_note: Present in the Android analyst, appsec, migration and explorer agent definitions; the design rule was added in v3.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: Grep-then-range reading rule, Analyst reading rules: ranged reads, one hop, own evidence, section 5.3

members.name: Agents audit run transcripts for wasted calls
members.problem: Briefs may waste calls or ignore their own rules, invisibly.
members.mechanism: Give an Opus pass the six lane transcripts, ask it to list wasted calls and ignored rules; the owner or Fable triages.
members.status_note: Refuted: recorded quota failures came from fan-out size and effort, not waste inside agents; fixed overhead dominates.
members.results: Not tested; the earlier transcript audit found nothing that caused a mistake.

members.name: Coverage ledger and stale-label freshness
members.problem: A derived index silently goes out of date when source files change, and nobody knows what was actually read.
members.mechanism: Per file version the ledger lists read and unread chunks and dangling endpoints; every query checks file hashes; changed-file records are labelled STALE; refresh keeps unchanged chunks and supersedes changed ones instead of deleting.
members.status_note: Manual command; tested on synthetic cases only; the changed-source case was designed but not run.
members.results: 4,053 dangling endpoints at L1/L2 and 3,673 at L3 (M); 5 'claim without attested premise' flags (M).

members.name: Hand-written reading-coverage ledger
members.problem: A report may claim sources were read when they were not; coverage needs to be visible.
members.mechanism: A file-by-file, page-by-page table recording what was read in full or sampled, with access limits and a verification record.
members.status_note: Hand-maintained; drifts.
members.results: 41 coverage rows checked by script on 2026-09-30 (M); effect on rework not yet measured.

members.name: Stale by code change, never by age
members.problem: A stored fix or finding goes stale when the code, version or platform it depends on changes; age is a poor stand-in (the board carried 183 minor findings with no status).
members.mechanism: Each entry lists typed dependencies (file blob hashes, config keys, versions, environment probes). A changed item marks the entry suspect and its check re-runs; if the control pair still flips, the trace is re-stamped (early cutoff) and the entry stays useful.
members.status_note: Section 3.5 and 5 of the knowledge-store design and part of the v2 library; symbol-level spans wait for KS-6b, whole-file hashes until then. D12 lean: findings go stale on code change.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: footprint, trace, early cutoff, lazy invalidation, B4 Staleness

members.name: Coordinator session that never implements
members.problem: With many sessions running at once, someone must own the plan, the shared results file, cross-lane contracts and the merge call without being buried in implementation or token cost.
members.mechanism: One Fable session on the plan branch owns the ship plan, W0-results.md, OWNER-VIEW.md, cross-lane contracts and the merge-readiness call on every PR. It writes and tags plan edits, dispatches binding reviews and does not implement.
members.status_note: Running since 2026-11-13; the coordinator built L1 and P0a-prep itself and runs the lane board.
members.results: Eight lane sessions woken and resumed after the power loss by the coordinator [M]. No measured effect on speed yet.

members.name: Lane sessions: one phase, own worktree, run in parallel
members.problem: Version 8 ran one phase at a time, so twelve days passed with nothing built while code phases waited behind the owner's first phase.
members.mechanism: Each lane is one Claude Code session (Opus lead) with its own git worktree cut from origin/main. It runs exactly one phase, ends in a draft PR titled with the phase id, and several lanes run at once.
members.status_note: Eight lane sessions started 2026-11-13 (P1, P2a, L2, P7a, P6a, P9-0a, P12a, L3a).
members.results: Eight lanes running on 2026-11-13 (M); PRs #187-#192 opened that day (M). RAM, not CPU, sets the ceiling (M).

members.name: Lead implements the Opus work itself
members.problem: A long-lived orchestrator window that only briefs others was the largest measured token cost of the program, and every hand-off loses context.
members.mechanism: In a lane, the Opus lead reads the plan and implements the Opus-owned work itself; Sonnet subagents get tests, screens, read models, infra files and runbooks. Replaces 'the main session never implements' for lanes only.
members.status_note: Applied to every lane started 2026-11-13.
members.results: Not yet tested; the source only states the orchestrator window was the largest token cost (M).
members.aka: lead implements, Sonnet subagents do Sonnet-owned work

members.name: Fresh-agent cold-resume trial
members.problem: Nobody knows whether the repository alone carries enough state for a new session to resume work, with no memory of earlier sessions.
members.mechanism: A Sonnet agent given only the repository (plan-branch path plus a hand-off folder holding expected.json) must recover ten frozen facts about P1; the session judges each miss as absent, ambiguous or present-but-missed, citing the plan line, and edits the plan only for absent or ambiguous facts.
members.status_note: Trial once, as P1's first act; evidence goes under docs/program/evidence/resume-trial-P1/. The miss-classification rule is an adopt proposal. Not yet run in the sources.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: resume-trial-P1, cold-resume trial, expected.json hand-off, G2-F134

members.name: One-sentence source-precedence rule in ship plan
members.problem: When the journal, the plan on main, the Plan @ sha, a design note and CLAUDE.md disagree, a fresh agent has no stated order for which one wins.
members.mechanism: One sentence in ship-plan section 0, never in CLAUDE.md: for phase work, owner correction > plan on main > Plan @ sha > cited design note; for stack facts CLAUDE.md and code win; stricter plan rule beats looser invariant; other conflicts stop and ask.
members.status_note: Proposal; tested through the P1 cold-resume trial.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Honest cold-resume trial: hashed answer key
members.problem: The P1 cold-resume trial (can a fresh session resume the work) could pass just by the agent reading the answer file or changing files, so the test would prove nothing.
members.mechanism: Record sha256(expected.json) in the PR journal before the run; commit the file only after judging; never name its path where the agent reads; run on a checkout without the answer; check HEAD and worktree unchanged and that the read log shows the plan was read and the key was not. The 58-scenario suite was dropped.
members.status_note: Adopt, narrowed by the refuter; applies to P1's cold-resume trial (n=1, rerun once if contaminated).
members.results: not yet tested. Pass test: hash in journal before dispatch, zero reads of the key in the transcript, agent ran without the answer file.

members.name: Scripts before agents
members.problem: 38 of 71 practised ideas failed as prose lines in a brief and model re-checks.
members.mechanism: Models find things; scripts decide whether a finding is closed. The gate, audit, planner and parser spend no tokens.
members.status_note: Standing rule of the design.
members.results: Testbed: 33 [M] practised dropped ideas worked and 38 [M] failed, mostly as prose.
members.aka: Script before agent, spend no tokens

members.name: Run small tasks inline before spawning agents
members.problem: Every subagent pays about 7.5k tokens of project instructions plus the context block before working, so tiny tasks and per-claim agents waste spend.
members.mechanism: Counts, greps, hashes, git logs, docker checks and migration greps run inline in the main session and pass to agents as args; claims are batched per verifier; discovery agents return facts, not verdicts; verification only where it moves a decision.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed (cap sizes never quantified); applied in design v2 (cut H-04, H-05, S-02, O-09); pre-flight commands listed, awaiting Docker Desktop.
members.results: Not yet tested; overhead figure approximate (CLAUDE.md about 7.5k tokens). Clinic lane has no token or dollar figures (M: none); only check durations of 274-840 s.
members.aka: Overhead rule, tiny tasks inline, Section 4.1 pre-flight, Cut from v1: H-04, H-05, S-02, O-09, A1-08, Cost rules: inline first, facts not verdicts

members.name: Fixed context overhead measurement
members.problem: Each session or subagent carries tokens before doing any work, and it was not known how large that prefix is.
members.mechanism: A usage tool breaks down per-agent overhead (tools, MCP, skills, system prompt, memory); docs_evolution.py measures documentation growth and pre-reading load.
members.status_note: October snapshot; docs grew in November.
members.results: About 70k tokens before work: 70,021 summed (system tools 33,968; MCP tools 16,599; skills 9,059; system prompt 7,926; memory 2,469) (M). Docs 1,357,226 bytes, about 338,816 tokens at chars/4 (E).

members.name: Medium-vs-xhigh effort trial with pass bar written first
members.problem: Choosing a model tier and effort for reviewers and verifiers is guesswork; without a rule fixed in advance a comparison can be bent to the result, and same-model errors are correlated.
members.mechanism: Replay 12 frozen refuter/skeptic briefs with adjudicated verdicts at medium and xhigh, 3 times each, with an xhigh repeat as noise floor; pass bar written in the PR journal first (10+ confirmed, 5 refuted items; unknown tokens count as fail); fixtures from 5 closed defects, blind-graded.
members.status_note: Trial, one-off; no standing golden set; standing re-run on every model refuted. Several families downgraded to FixFlow-only; thirty or more shadow pairs add agents against the one budget. Applies only if the owner trials F034.
members.results: not yet tested; the testbed has no effort benchmark.

members.name: Medium-effort verifiers via blind paired shadow runs
members.problem: Most verifiers run at xhigh effort, which costs more; one outside report says medium often matched or beat xhigh.
members.mechanism: A second agent at medium on the same brief, model and input hash, blind to the incumbent, shadows each non-P0 verifier; at least 30 pairs, pre-registered pass bar, three repeats per arm, scored against final adjudication, pass per model id.
members.status_note: Top trial 1 in section 0; the addendum weakened the outside evidence (pairs ran on different dates and agent versions; he reads it as Opus-specific).
members.results: Not yet tested. Targets: agreement at least incumbent minus 1 (T); medium tokens at most 0.6x (T); no medium verdict flips a skip/refuted to adopt/trial.
members.aka: G4-F034, G4-F032, G4-F181, G4-F031, Blind paired shadow: medium vs incumbent verifier effort

members.name: Rerun knowledge-store refuter set at high effort
members.problem: It is unknown whether verifiers run at xhigh need to be that expensive.
members.mechanism: Rerun the committed knowledge-store refuter workflow on frozen inputs at Opus/high twice, comparing with the xhigh outcomes.
members.status_note: Conditional: only if G4-F203 shows xhigh verifier spend is at least 20%.
members.results: not yet tested.

members.name: Log context use at phase close (usage and peak context)
members.problem: The 500k context trigger (HR-C4) has no sensor, and it is unknown whether a fuller orchestrator window degrades its judgements; the 40% context rule is anecdotal.
members.mechanism: Fable calls get_usage('self') at phase close and records tokensUsed, percentUsed and compaction count, checked against per-call usage in one transcript. For 5 phases also record peak per-call context and the token position of each owner correction or reviewer reversal.
members.status_note: First 4 phase sessions for the usage line; 5 phases for the peak instrument. Instrument only; HR-C4 fires from it.
members.results: not yet tested; the 40% budget is anecdotal

members.name: Record weekly-window usage per phase
members.problem: HumanLayer's dollar figures do not fit a flat subscription where weekly usage limits bind, so the verifier spend share is unknown.
members.mechanism: Over P1-P3 the closing 'what evidence ran' line records weekly-window percent from get_usage at phase open and close, plus Workflow-reported subagent tokens and agents lost to a usage limit.
members.status_note: Trial, narrowed. Gates G4-F228: runs only if xhigh verifier spend is at least 20%.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Record true peak context and reversal positions
members.problem: A 40% context rule is untested here, and the on-screen context percentage includes the autocompact buffer, so decisions made at high context are mislocated.
members.mechanism: For 5 phase sessions a Haiku extractor reads the transcript JSONL, computes per-call context as input + cache_creation + cache_read tokens, records the peak per window and model id, and logs the context position of Fable decisions later reversed.
members.status_note: Trial, method corrected in the 2026-11-09 addendum.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Measurement ledger and pipeline M00-M06
members.problem: No standing way to measure whether harness changes help: all eight exports have null tokens, effort, cost and resume time.
members.mechanism: An append-only JSONL ledger with hash manifests and an identity hierarchy, an optional rebuildable SQLite index, and seven slices H00 and M00-M06; evaluation-run schema built in the clinic repository.
members.status_note: Designed, not built; the owner ruled it low priority (AGENTS.md:22); the review rated it skip (a month of clinic research showed no gain). M00/H00 must not start unless asked.
members.results: Not yet built. Audit: eight active exports with null provider tokens (M); three validator defects probed. The clinic research established no gain (per the review).
members.aka: M00-M06, A7-09, A7-10, A7-12, A7-09 to A7-12, evaluation-run schema

members.name: Standing per-stage token and cost attribution
members.problem: Spend is not attributed per stage, agent and model, so waste is hard to locate.
members.mechanism: Attribute tokens and cost per stage, agent and model from recorded counts at pinned rates; use tokens per solve as a codebase-health signal.
members.status_note: Skip after refutation: reopens the skipped M00-M06 measurement pipeline; per-agent data already sits in workflow transcripts.
members.results: Evidence was marketing, one anecdote and a hypothesis.

members.name: Cost envelope by stage
members.problem: Ultracode multiplies tokens across agents, so spend needs an order-of-magnitude expectation before running.
members.mechanism: A table of agents per stage and tier mix: W1 16 agents, W2 8 analysts, up to 8 citation checks, up to 12 skeptics, 1 web re-check, 0 agents at gates.
members.status_note: Orders of magnitude only, no actual spend recorded.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Secret-safe scans: fingerprint, never value
members.problem: Every agent output is journaled, so a pasted secret would be stored in the run journal.
members.mechanism: The dependency and secret scan returns file, pattern, line number, first commit and a hash fingerprint; it never returns the value or a quoted line and must not paste matches into its reasoning.
members.status_note: Output schema SCAN enforces it.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Keep secrets and customer data out of the store
members.problem: Entries could store secrets, phone numbers or customer data; everything an agent reads reaches Anthropic; raw symptom text in evidence tables would commit defect and customer data to GitHub.
members.mechanism: A local scrubber redacts live secrets, token and connection-string patterns, Pakistani phone and CNIC patterns, and fails closed on write. Names and addresses cannot be detected, so raw production output is never stored. Raw tables stay local; only scrubbed aggregates are committed.
members.status_note: Applies to KS-0, KS-1, KS-5, KS-9; a gitleaks second pass is an owner decision (D5).
members.results: Not yet tested; a known-miss fixture shows the name and address limit in every test run.
members.aka: scrubber, KS-F scrub rules, X-06, K19, D7, scrub

members.name: No secrets in skills: key names and fingerprints
members.problem: Agents reading eas.json, app.json or .env could copy real tokens or keys into skills, briefs or outputs.
members.mechanism: Files holding real values are referred to by path and key name only. A committed value is reported as a fingerprint (first 12 hex of its sha256), never the value or the line. Agent definitions forbid opening .env files.
members.status_note: Written into every agent definition read in this lane.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Replacement graph test with a real engine
members.problem: The first graph test used the weakest query and no real engine, so it could not tell us whether a repo graph helps.
members.mechanism: Facts, algorithm, output form and engine are varied separately; sealed tasks from 140 commits (65 tune, 75 held out) and 50 questions; hops 1 to 6; a search baseline; a SQLite arm; a graph engine once chosen.
members.status_note: Protocol frozen, build under way at the time of the compile; inconclusive likely. Sibling records report the held-out run later completed.
members.results: Hop 1 recall 0.38; hop 2 0.72; hop 3 0.87 (M). Typed path returns 4 tables where untyped search returns 254 nodes (M).

members.name: Typed symbol-level graph of the repo
members.problem: Answer 'what else must change with this code' with a short ranked list, using typed links across web, mobile and backend that a flat search or import list cannot follow.
members.mechanism: A model-free script extracts about 2,500 symbols and 19+ edge kinds (calls, imports, routes, client URL calls, table reads and writes, settings, outbox kinds, tests, doc citations, co-change) at each task's parent commit; queries run with hop budgets and ranking. Frozen protocol: 140 task commits, 65 TUNE, 75 HELD-OUT.
members.status_note: Facts and sealed tasks built, tuned on 65 June commits, run once on 75 held-out commits (2026-11-13), three refuters done. Narrow result: no agent was run. The research-results doc's 'held-out not yet run' wording is out of date.
members.results: Held-out recall of reference files inside an 8,000-token answer: typed 0.700 +- 0.022 (M) vs scripted search 0.625 and co-change floor 0.638 (M). Typed minus search +0.076 [0.036, 0.118] (M); gain sits on mobile seeds +0.151, backend +0.012 and web +0.025 include zero (M). TUNE: relational = LadybugDB = DuckPGQ 0.7843 (M).
members.aka: typed property graph, tuned repo graph, replacement graph test, graph2, repo graph test with a frozen protocol

members.name: File-level connection graph (first test)
members.problem: Could a graph with a cache on top cut tokens and lookup steps by answering 'what depends on this file' in one small answer?
members.mechanism: A script with no model builds a file-to-file graph (imports by name, test mocks, docs citing files) as JSON or a SQLite table and answers 'everything that depends on this file'.
members.status_note: Rejected by the owner as naive; its 'no graph' verdict was withdrawn the same day. Superseded by the typed symbol-level graph test and the contract map.
members.results: 618 files, 1,119 links, 197 KB, 0.2 s build (M). Import links matched an independent method on 441/441 Python and 678/678 JS/TS pairs (M). Answered 1 of 200 searches fully and saved no step; one query tops out at recall 0.25 (M). Answer about 560 tokens vs about 200 for one search (E).
members.aka: graph/, connection index, graph database with a cache on top

members.name: Archive policy and reaper for worktrees and containers
members.problem: Worktrees (19), sessions and containers (34) pile up and eat memory.
members.mechanism: A written archive rule and a dry-run reaper that only lists merged, clean worktrees and their compose projects, skipping anything written in the last 24 hours or with an open session.
members.status_note: Lists only; the owner approves each batch. Compile class: Decide.
members.results: 34 containers; 25 of 26 clinic databases stopped; 19 worktrees (M).
members.aka: B15, B15 remedy, clean-up, worktree reaper

members.name: Archiving and progress-visibility rules
members.problem: The owner relies on one large board file, and sessions pile up.
members.mechanism: The root archives nothing without the owner's word. Each slice gets a board row, and a task.md holds status and next action.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed; no live status mechanism was found.
members.results: Board is 219,111 bytes (M); 19 worktrees (M).

members.name: Proposed: expiry list and progress file
members.problem: Idle worktrees and containers pile up, and progress is invisible.
members.mechanism: An automatic expiry list plus a short progress file that each session writes every N minutes.
members.status_note: Not built.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Pre-commit hook running workflow verify
members.problem: Broken links, bad JSON, provenance errors or workflow-test failures get committed because nothing checks them at commit time.
members.mechanism: tools/git-hooks/pre-commit runs coding_workflow.py verify (links, fences, provenance JSON, PDF hashes, instruction contracts, 29 workflow tests); a disposable-clone script proves reproduction from a committed HEAD. Local and bypassable.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed (configured per checkout); rejected for FixFlow because it had RT-04/05 defects (reads the working tree, not staged bytes; treats 'Ran N tests' as success so an all-skipped suite passes, RT-01) and CI gates the PRs.
members.results: 227 tracked files byte-identical to committed blobs; 29 workflow tests pass; all ten Git validations pass; broken-link and bad-interpreter commits rejected (M). It checks documents, not application behaviour.

members.name: Checkpoint and resume by dependency hash
members.problem: After a stop, an agent cannot tell which files it relied on have changed, so it either trusts a stale handoff or re-reads everything. Work is lost or redone.
members.mechanism: A stdlib Python tool (tools/coding_workflow.py) hashes task.md, a context packet and chosen source files into a JSON checkpoint; resume re-hashes and lists changed or deleted dependencies. Unrelated changes do not invalidate it. A verify command and pre-commit hook sit beside it.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed with eight red-team defects open. For FixFlow the Python tool was skipped on 1 Nov and the git-based Plan @ sha was adopted instead (superseded there by Plan @ sha).
members.results: Pilot: fresh checkpoint accepted, unrelated change accepted, stale dependency rejected; 24 reader calls, 6 packet-preparation reads; 29 behaviour tests pass (M). 8 red-team defects still open (M). Whole-file granularity; does not resume a halted session.
members.aka: A7-02, A7-04, A7-13, verify command and pre-commit hook, Python checkpoint hashing and resume freshness, Checkpoint and resume freshness check

members.name: Per-lane gate harness with Docker recipe
members.problem: A gate script reporting only the last exit code hides which gate failed; version 8 allowed only one backend phase at a time to run Docker gates, blocking parallel lanes.
members.mechanism: ff-gates.sh backend|mobile|web runs each gate (ruff, mypy, import-linter, alembic, pytest, pip-audit) in a container named for its lane with its own database, read-only source copy, per-gate logs, GATE lines with exit codes, summary.txt, run in the background.
members.status_note: Designed in the orchestration design (Appendix A, hardened v3); built as ff-gates.sh in phase L1; baselines green on main's code 2026-11-13 and used by every lane.
members.results: Backend 757 tests, 0 skipped, 7 min 23 s cold (M); web 106 tests, 33 s (M); mobile 334 tests, 29 s warm (M).
members.aka: ff-gates.sh, L1 parallel gate harness, Appendix A, S-07b, gate stack

members.name: Gates share the database container's network
members.problem: Another project's 29 networks exhausted Docker's address pools, so docker network create failed and the first gate design could not run.
members.mechanism: Gate containers join the database container's network namespace (database at localhost, as in CI); anything needing a real network declares an explicit subnet inside 10.77.0.0/16. FixFlow never prunes networks it did not create.
members.status_note: Fixed in commit be2e27a; design Appendix C still cannot run as written.
members.results: Error 'all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted' measured 2026-11-13 (M); fixed by this change.

members.name: Android toolchain in a user folder, verified on disk
members.problem: The device lab and P0a need a JDK, adb, apksigner, an emulator and a system image on this PC without changing system settings.
members.mechanism: Install into C:/Users/User/.fixflow-cache/android, loaded per terminal via env.sh, nothing on PATH, uninstall by deleting the folder. The installer reports success only for files found on disk, after its first run printed 'INSTALL OK' with nothing installed.
members.status_note: Installed 2026-11-13; 8.6 GB on disk; one DLL absent (see antivirus idea).
members.results: JDK 17.0.21, adb 1.0.41, build-tools 37.0.0, emulator 37.2.13, Android 14 image, AVD ff34 installed (M); 'WHPX is installed and usable' (M).

members.name: L3 device lab on a native emulator
members.problem: Drain logic and field-reliability steps meet a real phone holding real data with no earlier rehearsal, and Docker has no /dev/kvm to run an emulator.
members.mechanism: A native emulator on Windows Hypervisor Platform with three scripted protocols: drain rehearsal (L3a), adb-scriptable O-01 steps (L3b) and the offline matrix (L3c). A lab backend serves edge-404, 5xx or hang stand-ins; no lab build can reach a real server.
members.status_note: L3a started 2026-11-13, stacked on L2; L3b and L3c later. Emulator boots on this PC (Android 14 under WHPX, lab app installed) per a recent commit.
members.results: Not yet tested; every check must be shown failing once.
members.aka: device lab, L3a, L3b, L3c, emulator rig, L3

members.name: Secrets and private data kept out of agents' reach
members.problem: Sessions holding production credentials could leak secrets, or act on injected text in fetched pages. Subagents in bypass mode can reach Railway and GitHub credentials in the user profile.
members.mechanism: Pass secrets by variable name only; committed records name the variable not the value; agents never read .env. Define a restricted research agent type (Read, Grep, Glob, web only, no Bash) plus deny rules for ~/.ssh, ~/.railway, GitHub CLI and dump folders; canary-test it.
members.status_note: G1-F046 adopt, G5-F024 trial (narrowed to cutting the private-data leg; stands after the addendum). FixFlow-only: the testbed holds no production credentials and records no leak.
members.results: Not yet tested here. First check is a ten-minute canary in a bypass-mode Workflow.
members.aka: G1-F046, G5-F024, restricted research agent, lethal trifecta cut

members.name: Secrets passed by variable name in briefs
members.problem: Phases that handle secrets (backup dump, Cloudflare access calls) could leak secret values into committed records, PR bodies or agent context.
members.mechanism: In P0a, P3b, P3c and P4a briefs, secrets are passed by variable name (PGPASSWORD, $CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET); records name the variable never the value; agents never Read or cat a .env file.
members.status_note: Proposal; applies to four named phases only.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Per-checkout isolation
members.problem: Parallel sessions collide on branches, ports and test databases; two runs of one checkout dropped each other's test database.
members.mechanism: Each slice has its own git worktree, branch, compose project, database port and database names suffixed with a hash of the checkout path; a second check of the same checkout is refused; shared documents are read-only for slices.
members.status_note: In use; costs one database container per checkout. The source suggests one shared database container with per-checkout databases (separate idea).
members.results: No collision count. Recorded failure: two runs of one checkout dropped each other's test database, 115 errors (M). 19 worktrees exist (M).

members.name: Per-checkout isolation
members.problem: Parallel agent branches collide on ports, databases and files.
members.mechanism: Each checkout gets its own worktree, branch, port, database and compose project.
members.status_note: In use.
members.results: Supported 432 commits and 65 merges in eight working days (M).

members.name: Screenshot-and-rubric pipeline for screens
members.problem: Screen quality is hard to check without a human looking.
members.mechanism: Capture screenshots and score them against a rubric.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed.
members.results: not stated

members.name: UI capture-and-rubric pipeline
members.problem: UI changes need visible before/after evidence.
members.mechanism: A capture script screenshots every role and screen at 375 and 1280 px with a manifest; an Opus rubric review and refutation score the results.
members.status_note: Model scores are triage only.
members.results: 130 pages, 260 PNGs, 12 MB (M); rubric 64/160 to 110/160; of 59 findings: 16 fixed, 20 partly, 22 not, 1 regressed (M).

members.name: Tiered verification and rework-rate metric
members.problem: Full suites each session cost time, and there is no health metric for review rework.
members.mechanism: Run a relevant test subset per phase with cheap proxies and the full suite at close; track the share of the diff changed after review (under 5% bar).
members.status_note: Skip: full gates at close already exist; Docker setup cost does not shrink with a subset; squash merges break the metric.
members.results: The 5% bar is an unmeasured rule of thumb.

members.name: Per-PR rework rate as health metric
members.problem: No measure shows whether review is converging or code keeps changing after review.
members.mechanism: Track the share of the diff changed after review per PR; under 5% is the quality bar.
members.status_note: Over the cap: no refuter verdict; reviewers split trial vs skip.
members.results: not yet tested; no verdict

members.name: Infrastructure failures kept apart from content failures
members.problem: A flaky provider or a run that tested nothing must not read as a pass or as a bad brief.
members.mechanism: A null is never a result; the section 4.3 breaker reads fresh nulls as a suspected session limit; zero tests run is never green; coverage must read 16/16 or carry a waiver.
members.status_note: Already program law.
members.results: Confirmed.

members.name: Circuit breaker on session limit
members.problem: When the account session limit is hit, issuing more agents only produces nulls and hides what did not run.
members.mechanism: Readers run in slices of five; two or more fresh nulls in one slice halts issuing, accounts for every unstarted id as not_started, logs HALT and returns.
members.status_note: Added in v2, hardened in v3 (not_started list).
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Choose candidate fixes by an executed check
members.problem: Picking among several candidate answers by vote alone resolves fewer issues than picking by a test that runs.
members.mechanism: Generate several candidates (fixes, explanations, paths) and keep the one that passes an executed check such as a reproduction test or regression filter.
members.status_note: The one thought-structure with evidence; mapped to CureFound's explain-and-verify.
members.results: 25.7% resolved by vote alone, 27.0% with a regression filter, 32.0% with a reproduction test (S).

members.name: Several candidate fixes chosen by executed test
members.problem: A single fix often creates a new defect.
members.mechanism: Generate three candidate fixes per recorded chain; a frozen pre-written test plus a guard-removal check rejects the candidate that causes the defect.
members.status_note: Trial in the compile (replay first; live only if the selector works); deferred in v2, not run unless the owner switches it on after the contract's replay.
members.results: Outside: 25.7 % vote, 27.0 % with regression filter, 32.0 % with generated tests on SWE-bench Lite (S). Not tested here.

members.name: Phase-close scan for fixes stranded off main
members.problem: A fix can be stranded off main (a Sentry fix pushed after its PR merged), and a scan that waits for a flip back never sees it.
members.mechanism: At every phase close each validated entry's probe runs at origin/main; any PRESENT is reported as 'fix not on main' or 'regression'. ks close prints four counts, anchors branch shas by patch-id and pushes events in one turn.
members.status_note: Phase KS-3b.
members.results: not yet tested. Fixture must fire at every main tip from b4f0766 to ded44c8 [T].

members.name: ks close at phase end: anchor, rescan, four counts
members.problem: Fixes can be pushed after their PR merged and stay stranded off main; entries drift after refactors.
members.mechanism: One command re-points controls to the squash commit by patch-id, reads blobs at origin/main, re-runs declarative probes, labels results 'fix not on main' or 'regression', re-runs the diff lookup over the merged commit, syncs, and prints four counts.
members.status_note: Section 5.2; not built.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: ks close, phase close scan, KS-F13

members.name: Caller-pin test in repository CI (D17)
members.problem: A new file could mint a login token without calling the lock check, and no store lookup or protective test can see that second door.
members.mechanism: A backend pytest using stdlib ast pins the allowed callers of verify_pin and create_access_token to IdentityService.login. Validated trap probes (eas.json, app.json) may also be promoted into repository CI.
members.status_note: Needs no store; can land as its own PR any time before ship phase P7b-1; an owner to-do item, not a store feature.
members.results: not yet tested.
members.aka: D17, KS-O5, KS-O6, KS-P15, ITIL permanent fix

members.name: Lessons become checks
members.problem: The same defects arrive repeatedly and notes alone do not stop them (38 of 71 practised ideas failed as prose, per the v2 design). A lesson that needs a lookup can be missed.
members.mechanism: An entry seen three times is proposed as a lint, test or gate clause; its mechanical check is promoted into the shared tests every piece of work passes. Once it lands the entry retires and the gate catches the mistake with no lookup.
members.status_note: Library mechanism, later in the build order; modelled as its own pathway; one real instance already protects today (f10-1b).
members.results: Model: catches 0.04 [G] more pieces per 100 at middle values, 2.8 [G] at all-good. Real case f10-1b: an empty-value check blocks the mistake for every agent [M]. Left out of the model: a bad entry's check can pin a defect.
members.aka: Entry retires into a lint, test or gate clause, drains into CI, D17, promoted checks

members.name: Tree, Forest and Graph of Thoughts
members.problem: Could structured multi-branch reasoning improve agent results over a single chain?
members.mechanism: Branch and merge multiple reasoning paths in a tree, forest (several trees by consensus) or graph before answering.
members.status_note: Rejected as named methods; one narrow exception (candidate fixes chosen by executed check) is worth a replay at frozen commits.
members.results: Outside: 4 % to 74 % on a number puzzle (GPT-4, 2023) at several times the compute [S]; no gain beyond plain sampling at equal compute on current models [S]. Not tested here.

members.name: Thought structures (tree, forest, graph, debate, vote)
members.problem: A hoped-for way to improve agent output and fixes.
members.mechanism: Tree, forest and graph prompt layers, tree-search agent with model judge, voting over findings, debate loops, model merging of slices, one full check per candidate fix.
members.status_note: Gains were on puzzles with a 2023 model; at equal compute plain sampling matches them; they multiply calls and check queue. Three-candidate-fix replay stays the owner's to switch on (D20).
members.results: Not built; not tested here.

members.name: Pipelined verification per analyst
members.problem: Waiting for all analysts before checking leaves wall-clock time idle.
members.mechanism: Citation checks start as each analyst finishes; the fleet drain analyst O-10 is pipelined after O-03.
members.status_note: W2 script shape.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Citation check over every claim
members.problem: Analyst claims may quote text that moved, was fixed or never existed; agent research may misquote sources.
members.mechanism: A Sonnet agent per analyst re-locates each quote by content, checks git log and changed files, and marks LOCATED, MOVED, DEAD_CITATION or ALREADY_FIXED; existence only, behaviour is the skeptic's question. A research variant has a deterministic reducer re-fetch sources and exact-substring-check quotes.
members.status_note: Used at G2 and the plan delta check; the clinic research pack used a quote reducer for a 3-day procedure. It checks that a quote exists, not that the finding is right.
members.results: 109 claims re-located, none dead, none already fixed, some line drift (M). Clinic: 575 of 579 quotes verified by exact match; 4 unverified from one unfetchable source (M).
members.aka: Sonnet citation pass, CITATIONS schema, claim re-location, A6-02

members.name: Number tags (M, E, G, S) on every figure
members.problem: Readers cannot tell measured numbers from guesses.
members.mechanism: Tag every number as measured (M), estimated (E), guess (G) or outside study (S), with T target and I illustrative added by the harness.
members.status_note: Used across the program documents.

members.name: Evidence tags and honest labels on every fact
members.problem: Readers cannot tell how strongly a fact is established; reports blur observed, inferred, proposed and never-checked, and automated review is mistaken for human review.
members.mechanism: Every claim cites path:line with a quote and is tagged VERIFIED-IN-CODE, VERIFIED-BY-COMMAND, WEB (fetched this run) or INFERRED (clinic variant: REPORTED/OBSERVED/DOCUMENTED/INFERRED/PROPOSED/UNKNOWN); agents return facts, not severity, unless the schema asks; unknown is not zero.
members.status_note: A convention; nothing enforces it beyond schema nullability. Clinic labels were wrong at least twice and produced very long limit paragraphs.
members.results: Labels wrong at least twice in the clinic (restore run replaced; needle count 9 vs 55) (M). Otherwise not measured.
members.aka: VERIFIED-IN-CODE, VERIFIED-BY-COMMAND, WEB, INFERRED, evidence-status vocabulary, source_kind

members.name: Fit-screen the idea sweeps against bottlenecks
members.problem: Both idea sweeps scored ideas against the FixFlow ship plan, never against the 21 bottlenecks, so their verdicts could not be carried over.
members.mechanism: Opus mappers placed 87 kept ideas, Sonnet readers screened 868 dropped ones, Opus adjudicators ruled on 142 flagged, refuters attacked 51 claimed fits (default: no fit), a script checked every id, a last pass recomputed numbers.
members.status_note: Ran as three workflows, 19 agents; models reading documents, nothing run on the testbed except the token tally. One Sonnet pass screened the dropped Horthy families, so a missed idea stays missed.
members.results: 87 kept: 29 fit (2 direct, 27 supporting), 58 FixFlow-only. 868 dropped: 142 flagged, 91 restate, 1 promoted (R-05), 50 stay dropped. Of 142, the testbed had practised the mechanism in 71: 33 worked, 38 failed (M).
members.aka: section 9 mapping, FIT-LIST, re-screen of dropped ideas

members.name: Assess, refute by default, then judge (idea sweeps)
members.problem: Judging 1,906 sweep cards fairly, without the orchestrator scoring anything itself; a single reader's enthusiasm can promote weak ideas.
members.mechanism: Cluster cards into families; two Opus reviewers (benefit-seeking lens A, skeptic lens B) score each on five axes 0-3; a fresh-context Opus xhigh refuter attacks every adopt or trial family with default verdict refuted; a judge applies the rule; a completeness critic lists unread items.
members.status_note: Run on the BAML sweep (89 cards) and twice on the Horthy sweep (first pass and addendum). Whether default-refuted earns its cost is what trial G4-F034 would show.
members.results: Horthy: of 144 attacked families, 65 refuted and 79 narrowed, none passed (M); lenses agreed on 669 of 838 (M); addendum changed no disposition (M). BAML: adopt 24 to 0, trial 22 to 4; of 46 sent, 34 refuted, 11 downgraded, 1 survived (M).
members.aka: review pipeline, sweep pipeline, two-lens review

members.name: Skip-aware integration gate
members.problem: A test run reports green while integration tests were silently skipped because the database variable was unset, so the check proves nothing about the real database.
members.mechanism: pytest writes a junit report with skip reasons; a small script fails the gate if any integration test was skipped; pytest-style flags -rs used; --passWithNoTests removed from mobile CI.
members.status_note: Adopted in review (P1 and Appendix A); now part of every backend gate run. The skip-all behaviour when the database variable is unset is code-verified (conftest.py:65-72).
members.results: Baseline: 0 integration tests skipped of 757 (M).
members.aka: fail on skipped integration tests, fail when integration tests were skipped

members.name: AI review bots and unmeasured-as-failure policy
members.problem: Review bots add noise; missing scans must not count as clean; hand-back text could inject instructions.
members.mechanism: A per-PR Opus reviewer already exists; skip-aware gates treat unmeasured as failed; Claude Code labels a subagent's final report as model output with no user authority.
members.status_note: Already done or platform behaviour.

members.name: Typed output schemas, forced and validated
members.problem: Free prose from agents is costly to read, invites unchecked claims and guesses when blocked; the orchestrator and scripts need objects with a fixed shape.
members.mechanism: Each agent returns a JSON Schema object (MAP, RESEARCH, FINDINGS, VERDICT, COMMANDS and others), pure extractors with additionalProperties:false. The Workflow schema option forces a validated StructuredOutput call with retry. A blocked agent returns a named code and questions, never a guess.
members.status_note: Twelve schemas written in design section 5.2; referenced by all 11 agent definitions on PR #185; forced-output route is how the harness already works.
members.results: Strictness has no silent-drop failure; BAML's lenient repair route has a documented one (issue #4590) [S].
members.aka: Output schemas, Named output schemas and blocked codes, design 5.2 schemas, P-01, I-12, D-08, B-03, I-07, I-08, P-07

members.name: Pure prompt-input boundary for the skeptic
members.problem: A skeptic must see only claim, evidence and failing condition; nothing structural stops impact, fix_sketch, confidence or severity leaking into its prompt.
members.mechanism: skepticInput(finding) returns exactly {claim, evidence, failing_condition}, with a replay test that the rendered prompt contains none of the forbidden fields. About 10 lines.
members.status_note: Trial, unrefuted. Hygiene, not a fix: no contaminated skeptic is on record.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Short stable handles instead of hashes
members.problem: Agents echoing long ids or SHAs can mis-aggregate silently.
members.mechanism: Agents use short labels (H-01, S-07b); long hashes are checked by git in code so a mis-echo fails loudly.
members.status_note: Already done.
members.results: Outside measurement: small n, two runs per arm [S].

members.name: Numbered evidence ids for verifiers
members.problem: A verifier could cite a fabricated URL or quote.
members.mechanism: Number the evidence handed to verifiers and skeptics; they cite ids and the script rejects unknown ids.
members.status_note: Conflicts with the design: REFUTED needs counter-evidence the skeptic finds itself; the citation check already catches fabrication.
members.results: Not tested; no fabricated URL on record in a verification step.

members.name: Bounded session tree: depth three, fan-out three
members.problem: A large build needs structure so many sessions run without losing work or colliding.
members.mechanism: Root (Fable) holds the board and judges gates; slice leads on Opus or Sonnet; Haiku/Sonnet/Opus subagents; model and effort passed on every start; depth root-slice-child-subagent; at most three running children per node; one file set per node; state in task.md.
members.status_note: Rationale asserted, not measured.
members.results: No cost or time comparison with another structure. 12 slices and about 20 follow-up branches merged in 8 days [M]. Root became a serial gate; board reached 219,111 bytes.
members.aka: A8-05, Orchestration rules: tiers, depth 3, fan-out 3, state in repo

members.name: Bounded session tree, one file set per node
members.problem: Keep many parallel sessions from colliding on files, flooding the one reviewing parent, or exhausting the shared account session limit.
members.mechanism: Depth root, slice sessions, one child level, then subagents (depth three). At most three running children per node. Each node owns one file set, worktree and branch; siblings never share files; merges flow upward in dependency order.
members.status_note: Used throughout the clinic build; three running children was the practical limit with the staging rig.
members.results: No measurement (M: none). One incident: the notebook reconciliation hit the shared session limit once. The 400-character-per-turn handoff figure is asserted, not measured; 20 idle sessions still piled up (B08).
members.aka: A1-02, Session tree, depth three, fan-out three

members.name: Plan-check section in the orchestration document
members.problem: The orchestration document has no dependency graph, footprint check or lane arithmetic; capacity facts are stated as rules.
members.mechanism: Add the plan check as a new section after its second gate, lane arithmetic in its cost section and machine limits in constraints; rule: no plan runs before it passes.
members.status_note: Nothing changed; belongs to the ship plan's PR.
members.results: Not yet written.

members.name: Plan check: footprints, two graphs, refuse collisions
members.problem: Slices ran in parallel with nothing checking for collisions; the first check on merged main failed for the first two slices because of hand edits to shared documents.
members.mechanism: Each slice declares files written, interfaces read, prerequisites, shared things (migration number, port, database), risk and size. Build a needs-graph and a collides-graph; refuse plans with two writers of one file and branches touching outside their footprint; feed real touches back.
members.status_note: Spec complete (8 steps). The testbed never laid slices out with footprints, so there is no real plan to replay; the sample plan is made up.
members.results: Not yet tested. The testbed's first-check failures on merged main for the first two slices were hand-edit collisions [M].
members.aka: Parallel work is planned, not discovered, Footprint declaration, Collision graph

members.name: Saved script for the PR-review stage
members.problem: The PR-review stage is prose steps, so SHA binding and the per-id fail/pass table depend on the agent; workflows are rewritten each time.
members.mechanism: Commit one Workflow script taking {registerIds, headSha}, calling fixflow-pr-reviewer with a VERDICT schema carrying head_sha and per-id fail_on_base_test and pass_on_head_test, comparing SHAs in code.
members.status_note: After P1; chips at W5.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Gate review as workflow with typed verdict
members.problem: One root session is the serial gate: it briefed reviewers, read the last diff, ran the check twice and edited the board by hand; nothing could leave faster than the root.
members.mechanism: Reviewers run in a saved workflow, one gate at a time, writing reports to disk and returning a typed verdict naming the commit they read. Tested first with stand-in agents, after a probe that a workflow agent can run the check at all. The root keeps judgment.
members.status_note: Phase 3 of harness v2; rated trial in the compile. A script may refuse a merge only after the owner says so.
members.results: Not yet tested. Gain bounded: the root is 15.3 % of tokens (M).
members.aka: B04 remedy, Root as the only gate, Gate workflow and merge queue

members.name: Orchestration contract skill for the main session
members.problem: The main session must recall tier routing, the CONTEXT block, output schemas, script contract and session rules each phase without re-reading long design docs.
members.mechanism: An authored skill the main session (Fable) loads each phase: routing table, fixflow-* agentType registry, CONTEXT block, schemas, briefing and reading rules, W1/W2 script contract, plan section 0 rules. Not preloaded into subagents.
members.status_note: Authored; on PR #185, not merged.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Orchestration skill and repo-conventions skill
members.problem: Every session's agents need identical briefs, and implementers need deploy traps, migration numbering and slice boundaries aimed at them.
members.mechanism: A project skill carries the CONTEXT block, schemas, reading rules and routing table; a second skill packages CLAUDE.md plus handoff section 2 for implementation sessions.
members.status_note: Planned in section 9 of the orchestration document; the orchestration skill is referred to as existing in the Horthy sweep (fixflow-orchestration), but this record shows no build confirmation.
members.results: Not yet tested.
members.aka: FixFlow orchestration skill, FixFlow repo conventions

members.name: Give sweep assessors the design text and RT rules
members.problem: The assessment stage did not read the design documents, so eight of its 24 adopt calls were already program law and only the refuter caught it.
members.mechanism: For the next sweep, the assessment brief carries the section 5.2 text and the RT-01..RT-07 rules, or the orchestrator expects the refuter to do that work.
members.status_note: A note for the design's next edit; no change made.
members.results: Not yet tested. Observed cost: 8 of 24 adopts already done [M].

members.name: Reviewer-brief additions with no testbed counterpart
members.problem: FixFlow reviewers may miss deviations from the plan, unnamed config exceptions, over-engineering or design flaws; extra reviewer lines and a slow design audit target these.
members.mechanism: The compile's bundle of eight items: suppression and gate-config lists, deviations heading and report, seven defect shapes, a mechanical list of gate-defining files, and a design audit with a pass bar of two accepted findings.
members.status_note: Refuters downgraded G2-F077, G2-F104, G4-F089, G4-F186 and G4-F225 to FixFlow-only; G4-F225 would add a standing owner step against B03. Use G4-F073 (claims-file script) for the gate-file list instead.
members.results: not yet tested here.

members.name: Short tool list for gate agents
members.problem: Tool definitions are 34k tokens (M) of the roughly 70,000-token fixed cost per agent.
members.mechanism: A setting with a short tool list that always keeps Write; adopted only on a measured drop after a with-and-without test.
members.status_note: Designed in harness v2; adopt only on a measured drop. Context trials showed no gain from restoring.
members.results: Not yet run. Pass mark: 20 runs (T) with zero refused writes.

members.name: Strip the fixed prefix every agent pays
members.problem: Every subagent starts with about 60-70k tokens of tool schemas, connectors and instructions (tool definitions 34k), re-read on every call. Fan-out multiplies this prefix, not the work.
members.mechanism: Whitelist tools for high-volume gate agents (always keeping Write), defer tool schemas, connect fewer connectors, load no skills in agent sessions, use a generated board and short brief; adopt only after a with-and-without context reading.
members.status_note: Trial; a config line after an A/B. Whitelist always keeps Write (a list without Write caused refused writes, B16). Step 1: one /context reading; step 2: one workflow; per-phase MCP disable list only if eager MCP schemas are 20k tokens or more. Not built.
members.results: Not yet tested. Prefix about 60k (E) per the token report, about 70,000 (M) per v2, about 64k first-turn prompt (M) per the Horthy sweep; 56% of every agent's tokens (E); board 221 KB (M). Pass bar: 20 runs with zero refused writes (T).
members.aka: G1-F157, mechanism 11, lever 2, Tool allow-list for gate subagents, Whitelist tools for high-volume subagents, Short tool list for gate agents, Cut the fixed cost per agent, A small standing context, deferred tool schemas

members.name: Single aggregate pre-handoff check command
members.problem: No one named command runs typecheck, format and tests together as the gate before handoff, so agents can hand off with unchecked or noisy gate runs.
members.mechanism: Provide a single named aggregate check command (often parallel) called by both the routine and any hook. In FixFlow, named exit-coded gates already exist per runtime (Appendix A for backend, CLAUDE.md chains for web and mobile).
members.status_note: First pass: deferred, reviewers split. Addendum: already done per runtime; a cross-runtime aggregate does not fit a backend gated in Docker on Windows.
members.results: not yet tested; no verdict on a cross-runtime aggregate.
members.aka: G4-F005, G4-F002, Aggregate check and per-gate quiet exit codes

members.name: Quiet gate wrapper for web and mobile gates
members.problem: Verbose lint, test and build output floods the agent's window; the backend gate is already quiet but web and mobile are not.
members.mechanism: Extend the backend g() wrapper (full log to file, one EXIT line, pass/fail/skip counts, failure excerpt) to web and mobile gates, only if one green-run measurement shows output worth cutting; log gate-output tokens and truncated-tail re-runs.
members.status_note: Backend wrapper already in use; web/mobile extension is a trial over the first two code phases. FixFlow-only; the testbed's check already has a wrapper with heartbeat and watchdog, and every testbed context trial was null.
members.results: Core wrapper done for backend; web/mobile extension not yet tested.
members.aka: G1-F048, G4-F157, G4-F001, G4-F003, G4-F158, backpressure script

members.name: Survey of external memory and context tools
members.problem: Whether an existing hook, proxy or memory store could be adopted instead of building one, for example one that keeps about 800k tokens of history inside a 300-400k window.
members.mechanism: Source-pinned audit of about 20 outside tools (MemTree/Claude Code Infinite, Virtual Context, YesMem, LCM, Rolling Context, Distil, Parsec, Cairn and others) against that need; no installs or trials. Cairn writes a structured block into SQLite and pares tool definitions via a proxy.
members.status_note: None adopted; first pick was Infinite with MemTree, then superseded by the decision that no outside system is adopted and local hooks were built. Used as design vocabulary: summary DAG, topic hierarchy, expand-on-demand, stable cached prefix. One SQLite memory tool vendored as evidence.
members.results: None adopted (M). Vendor-reported only: MemTree 68.7 vs full history 69.3 vs native compact 48.7 (S); input 39M vs 113M vs 17M tokens (S); Parsec cost -39% (S); Distil 4.5 percent smaller prompts, 9.7 percent more cost (S). Not reproduced here.

members.name: Outside tools that cap tool output (CCH, Headroom, squeez and others)
members.problem: Find a shipped tool that bounds what tool outputs add to the window, or trims repeated reads.
members.mechanism: Static review of outside projects: PreToolUse hooks redirecting reads to shell helpers with a 25,000-token passthrough budget and stubbed large outputs; a proxy with a read-stale lifecycle; Rust updatedToolOutput rewriting; 19 pinned repos in all.
members.status_note: Each rejected as a complete remedy; none installed. CCH judged partial admission control; Headroom kept as comparator; squeez withdrawn. Usable parts kept: bypass list, stub-plus-retrieve cache, updatedToolOutput route.
members.results: No efficacy measured. Budget 25,000 estimated tokens per five-hour window (S); maintainer claim about 50% savings (S, not reproduced); bypasses found (stderr, small outputs, slices) (M, code reading); 69 source files hashed (M).
members.aka: claude-context-hooks, claude-context-manager, Headroom, squeez, context-mode, RTK, claude-mem, A6-15, A6-17, A6-18, A6-19

members.name: Cheap Haiku locator agent (fixflow-explorer)
members.problem: The built-in Explore agent inherits the session model's tier (Opus here), so a simple where-is-X lookup would run on the most expensive model.
members.mechanism: A project agent definition in .claude/agents/fixflow-explorer.md pins the model to Haiku and is used only for file-location lookups from a gate, not for reading or auditing.
members.status_note: The document states it is the only agent definition that existed at that point; later PR #185 added 11 more.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: fixflow-explorer: cheap Haiku locator
members.problem: The built-in Explore agent inherits the session model's tier, so a simple 'where is X?' costs more than needed.
members.mechanism: Read-only agent pinned to Haiku with Read, Grep, Glob, Bash. Greps first, reads at most 40 lines, reports path:line with the matching line, lists all definitions, no verdicts. Existed before PR #185.
members.status_note: File exists in the repo; no usage figures in the source.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Codex adapter: snapshot, restore and journal
members.problem: Keep exact task state across compaction in the local Codex tool, and show whether it beats native compaction.
members.mechanism: Seven hooks: PreCompact saves an immutable checksummed snapshot, compact-start restores it, a journal serves search and show, all under byte budgets; any failure degrades to native with a visible message.
members.status_note: Working restoration, tested over four runs; the line was stopped with 'unproven incremental value'.
members.results: Pilot input +10.31% vs native, score 100/100 both (M); final study recall 15/15 and task 100% in all arms, input +17.02% vs native and +6.08% vs notes (M); delivery gate failed at 4,962 B vs 4 KiB (M); 244 tests, 242 pass (M).

members.name: Snapshot before compaction, restore after (Codex adapter)
members.problem: After the context window is summarised, details are lost; native compaction may lose recall, so heavier machinery was tried.
members.mechanism: Snapshot state before compaction and restore it afterwards (checksummed), tried on another project built around OpenAI Codex, compared with a plain notes file and native compaction.
members.status_note: Three evaluations; final audit 'context gain proven: false'. A short notes file matched it; skip the heavy machinery for now, revisit only if a case shows recall loss.
members.results: Same recall (15 of 15) and task success in all arms; +6.1% tokens over a plain notes file and +17.0% over native compaction (M). Nothing here was shown to save tokens.
members.aka: A5-10 to A5-14, heavier context machinery

members.name: Journal of event files plus SQLite index
members.problem: Several sessions, worktrees and hosts must read and write one store safely, with full history and no lost writes, on Windows with no database server.
members.mechanism: Immutable, content-hashed (sha256) event files in a private git store are the truth; a disposable per-host SQLite file is a rebuildable projection with a watermark. No-replace publisher, freshness check, deterministic fold, commit lease, backup and restore.
members.status_note: Specified in section 3.1; build phase KS-1 (Opus implements) waits for the D1b yes and an idle Opus. Tested with 8+ processes and 1,000+ writes when built.
members.results: Not yet built as a system. Measured on this box: rename-over-existing failed 99-126 times per 8x1,000 identical events (M); freshness check 23-35 ms at 5,000 events (M). Refuters measured about 18,300 writes from about 1,500 processes with no corruption (M).
members.aka: journal + index, two layers, KS-1, tools/ks core, KS-A2, KS-R1, journal-first store

members.name: SQLite via node:sqlite as the knowledge-store engine
members.problem: Choose a store engine that needs no install, daemon or telemetry and runs on a Windows dev box and a Linux VPS for a few hundred rows.
members.mechanism: SQLite built into Node 24 (FTS5 for BM25 and trigram, JSON, WAL), one file per host outside all worktrees, SQLite 3.51.3 or later. Postgres, DuckDB, better-sqlite3, Meilisearch, sqlite-vec stay in reserve behind an abstraction layer.
members.status_note: A bounded engine trial was rejected: no two candidates were close.
members.results: WAL multi-process test: 4 writer processes, 12,000 rows, integrity ok (M). Graph-style lineage queries 0.07-95 ms (M).
members.aka: engine choice, one engine one form one CLI, KS-R6

members.name: Missed-existing detector with blind re-rule
members.problem: A miss of an existing entry looks the same as a store never consulted, so recall, wording-gap rates and the need for embeddings cannot be measured.
members.mechanism: At record time the author names preceding lookups; the CLI runs three detectors over the roster, computes a cause class (handle_gap, typo, vocabulary, threshold), and the author rules same/related/new. The reviewer re-rules blind. Unknown shows as NULL, never zero.
members.status_note: Built in KS-2 and KS-3 (sections 7.3, 4.5), read at KS-9; a lower bound by construction.
members.results: Not yet tested. Expected count below about 0.2 per 8-week window (E).
members.aka: v_missed_existing, KS-O17, same/related/new ruling, KS-P16..P22, missed_check

members.name: Misses are written down; lookup keys fixed
members.problem: A lookup library that fails silently never improves, and nobody knows when it should have answered.
members.mechanism: When a session solves what the library already held, record the miss and its cause and fix the lookup keys. The lookup table counts hit or miss and tokens returned.
members.status_note: Stop rule carried over: fewer than 3 verified hits in 20 encounters or 8 weeks [S].
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Send-back repeat share
members.problem: Unknown how often review send-backs repeat an earlier finding class.
members.mechanism: Count the share of review send-backs that repeat a class already found earlier.
members.status_note: Proposed; not run.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Review findings fed forward by slice type
members.problem: Review sends work back often and some findings repeat an earlier finding class, so the same fix round is paid again.
members.mechanism: Store review findings by slice type and serve them to builders of the next slice of that type.
members.status_note: The proposed no-build test is the share of send-backs that repeat an earlier finding class.
members.results: Not yet tested. Record: 2.8 [M] review rounds per slice, 64 % [M] sent back.

members.name: Adjudication record so later sessions can disagree
members.problem: Later sessions would re-run everything if the reasons for decisions were not kept.
members.mechanism: G2 writes the conflicts the orchestrator adjudicated and why, so a later session can disagree with reasons instead of re-running; the verified register and open-risks list are also kept.
members.status_note: Part of G2 output.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Verified register, open-risks list and refuted list
members.problem: A single pass/fail list loses unsettled claims and hides refutations; findings need a uniform record of how well each is verified and how severe.
members.mechanism: The script derives from verdicts a verified register (CONFIRMED, PARTIALLY), an open-risks list (UNVERIFIABLE, overflow, DEAD_CITATION, each with what would settle it) and a refuted list; Fable spot-reads every refuted P0. Register ids carry severity P0-P3 and a status V, S, C, G or O.
members.status_note: Realised at G2 as the verified findings register; a P0 on the open list blocks work on its area.
members.results: 139 findings at G2 (M).
members.aka: three buckets at G2, V/S/C/G/O codes, severity P0-P3

members.name: Cross-session digest of hot files
members.problem: Cut re-reading across sessions of the same helper bodies, the form that could pay since in-window repeats are tiny.
members.mechanism: A durable digest returning something shorter than the lines for the most-read files, lasting across sessions (the knowledge store's ground, not a graph's).
members.status_note: Nothing has shown a shorter digest can stand in for the lines.
members.results: Not yet tested. 72 paths (3.3 %) hold half the fetched tokens; 294 paths read in five or more windows hold 73 % (M).

members.name: Hot-set digests of often-read files
members.problem: A quarter of tokens is fetched file content and a small group of files is re-read across sessions, while questions rarely repeat.
members.mechanism: Keep a short digest of the often-read files that stands in for reading their lines.
members.status_note: The hot set exists, but nothing has shown a short digest can replace the lines; one project, unproven.
members.results: 3.3% of paths (72) hold half the fetched tokens (E); paths read in 5+ windows hold 73% (E); 74% of fetched tokens went to files never edited (E); files are 65-76% of reading (E). Digest not tested; saving estimated 5-24% (E) after refuters cut a first-round 42% claim.
members.aka: hot set, shorter digest instead of lines, file digests

members.name: Rejected storage engines and memory products
members.problem: The owner asked that no decades-old problem be re-invented and no database be faked with Markdown; broad discovery had to rule alternatives in or out, including a server database holding the store.
members.mechanism: Each candidate was scored against local-only data, Windows, telemetry-off and one-developer cost. Cassandra, ClickHouse, Neo4j, Qdrant and hosted memory products were rejected or kept as references; a Postgres-container store (proposal B) was unreachable when Docker Desktop is off.
members.status_note: Rejected as components; Postgres, DuckDB and Dolt are reserve swap targets. All three judges rejected proposal B.
members.results: Verdicts only: Cassandra needs an 8 GB RAM floor and has a 5-7 orders-of-magnitude scale gap (S, vendor docs). Proposal B scored 222 of 360 (M) and contradicts ruling KS-R1.
members.aka: rejected alternatives, Cassandra, Neo4j, vector servers, hosted memory, proposal B, ks Postgres

members.name: Neo4j and other server graph engines
members.problem: Offer the market-standard graph database as a possible home for the repo graph and its algorithms.
members.mechanism: Neo4j Community (a JVM server), FalkorDB or Postgres with Apache AGE via Docker, loaded with the same typed facts.
members.status_note: Not installed. The compile says do not build a graph database server on a memory-short PC; a server adds 1 to 2 GB of memory.
members.results: not yet tested
members.aka: FalkorDB, Postgres with Apache AGE, graph database server

members.name: Zero-token index replay on recorded windows
members.problem: Decide cheaply whether an import-and-caller index earns a live trial, before spending agent tokens.
members.mechanism: Build the index at each recorded window's start commit, count lookup-only calls it would have answered, and check whether its list holds the files the window went on to edit.
members.status_note: Co-change is the weak half at 432 commits.
members.results: not yet tested

members.name: Index replay at zero tokens
members.problem: Sessions spend many calls only reading; nobody knows whether a code index would have answered them or listed the files later edited.
members.mechanism: At each recorded window's start commit build an import-and-caller index, count the lookup-only calls it would answer, and check whether its list holds the files the window went on to edit. Reads the clinic repo and transcripts, writes nothing.
members.status_note: Zero-token first test; live trial only if the replay says so. Pass marks (3 % of tokens, recall 0.8 [T]) await owner decision.
members.results: Not yet run. Co-change half is weak: only 432 commits (M) to learn from.

members.name: Scripted search baseline arm
members.problem: Compare every graph against what sessions do today (text search for the seed's names, paths and route strings).
members.mechanism: Scripted text search, one and two rounds; deliberately not an agent searching.
members.status_note: Called a scripted search; no agent was run.
members.results: Held-out T1 recall 0.625 +- 0.031 (M); s2 0.634 (M); median 6 to 8 lookups (M); TUNE 0.759 (M).

members.name: Slow grep-and-model search over optimised retrieval
members.problem: Choosing a retrieval design for code understanding.
members.mechanism: Reliable agentic search (grep plus a model) preferred over optimised retrieval; a learned reranker was rejected.
members.status_note: Matches current practice; the reranker is a skip.

members.name: Context packet query with frontier and gap lists
members.problem: Give a fresh agent a small, cited evidence packet by named start rather than whole documents.
