members.mechanism: cmap context/find/show/chain/gaps: breadth-first expansion within a token budget, each record with quote and file:lines, plus UNRESOLVED, FRONTIER and COVERAGE lines; an empty answer is never 'no dependency'.
members.status_note: Never compared with routed reading; a frontier-drop defect is a static suspicion, not reproduced.
members.results: No data on delivered tokens or task quality; extraction recall vs an earlier reading 0.523 exact, 0.588 exact-or-loose (M).

members.name: Compact context packet
members.problem: Fresh agents are given large documents; the question was whether a smaller, fact-checked packet gives the same result with fewer bytes and faster work.
members.mechanism: Freeze required facts first; build a compact projection and count bytes at the delivery boundary including preparation; a deliberately removed fact must be rejected. Then a real-agent trial with and without the packet and a stale checkpoint, in isolated clones with a frozen oracle.
members.status_note: Byte pilot on 6 synthetic cases; real-agent trial on one small synthetic task per condition, not randomised. No gain shown.
members.results: Bytes 10,010 baseline vs 7,947 treatment, about 20.6% smaller (M); all 24 facts kept. Real-agent trial: same acceptance, phase times 193.1 vs 194.7 min (M); tokens, cost and human effort null.

members.name: Linux container check, proposed as the gate
members.problem: Tests ran only on Windows while production is Linux, and the Windows-to-Docker database path made the check slow and hid Linux-only failures.
members.mechanism: The whole check runs in a pinned Debian 12 container on the database's network, 12 workers, on a hash-verified copy of the tree, with no fallback to native. Proposed: the container run becomes the gate; Windows runs only when host tooling changes.
members.status_note: Built and verified in the clinic testbed's last week; optional, not the gate. Designed into harness v2 phase 2 (owner decision D09); expect one fix-up round for order-dependent tests.
members.results: 2,246 tests: container mean 230.1 s vs native 367.2 s, about 1.5x faster, parallel pass 1.9x (M); 319-360 s vs 476 s on a loaded day (M). First Linux run: 2,171 of 2,173 passed; later 2 of 2,472 failed only on Linux (M). Image 2.28 GB, cold build 6 min 28 s (M).
members.aka: A3-11, A4-01, A4-02, A4-03, A8-03, container gate, Linux run, Container run as the gate

members.name: Slow-path diagnosis: Windows to Docker port
members.problem: Adding workers stopped helping; where did the time actually go?
members.mechanism: Measure machine, worker and VM CPU during a parallel pass, and per-query latency from Windows versus inside the container. The database-path fix FC-20 was dropped in favour of the Linux container.
members.status_note: Cause is inferred; the container run is the closest A/B.
members.results: Machine 42 percent of 24 processors; six Python workers 2.45 cores; trivial query 0.63 ms vs 0.13 ms (M). Serial pass 104-165 s, 36-40 percent of wall time, never split.

members.name: Parallel check with a database per worker
members.problem: The full test run took about 14 minutes, so every gate and every review round waited on one 855-second run, and one session's wait queued everyone behind it.
members.mechanism: pytest-xdist runs 6 workers, each with its own PostgreSQL test database, plus a single-process serial pass for race tests. Load distribution is used (loadfile hung when a worker died). The runner proves every test ran exactly once.
members.status_note: In use as the clinic testbed's check (native Windows). FixFlow could use the same shape; its backend uses pytest-asyncio so per-worker databases would be needed.
members.results: One process 855.2 s (1,953 tests); 6 workers plus serial pass mean 283.8 s over 12 runs, range 268.3-298.3 s, about 3.0x faster (M). Serial pass is 36-37% of wall time (M). 8 workers gain 3% over 6 (M). Check is CPU-bound, not flush-bound (M).
members.aka: A3-01, A3-02, A3-05, A3-12, A1-10, A8-01, A7-05, pytest-xdist parallel check, Two-pass parallel check

members.name: Worker sweep and per-second load sampler
members.problem: Pick worker and slot counts from measurement and see memory and CPU during checks and drills.
members.mechanism: Sweep workers (6, 9, 12, 16); sample whole-machine CPU and free memory every 5 s (2 s on the VM) to CSV; test a pair at once before approving a second slot; the rig samples per-process memory and database connections.
members.status_note: Used on checks and on the rig VM; not on the developer PC for crash diagnosis.
members.results: Parallel pass 6 workers 137.5 s, 12 workers 104.7-135.1 s; knee between 6 and 12 (M). Two container checks 266-267 s vs 220 s alone. Rig drill j: minimum available 1,075 MB, used at most 825 MB.

members.name: CI checks for known prose traps
members.problem: FixFlow's written warnings (non-ASCII secret compare crashing auth, empty eas.json env value, Sentry plugin in app.json) rely on being read; a lint rule makes each trap mechanical.
members.mechanism: Ruff banned-API rule (TID251) on hmac.compare_digest, allow-listed in core/security.py; an eas.json check for empty env values; an app.json check banning the Sentry plugin. CLAUDE.md prose stays. Also floated: railway deny rule, skill-frontmatter lint.
members.status_note: Adopt for the eas.json, Sentry-plugin and compare_digest checks (G1-F010/F011, G2-F031, G2-F045); railway deny and frontmatter lint are trial (G4-F008, G4-F125 lineage). Proposal only, nothing installed. FixFlow-only: no testbed bottleneck is a recurring known trap.
members.results: not yet tested; no testbed number would move.
members.aka: G1-F010, G1-F011, G4-F008, G2-F045, G2-F031, Ruff ban on hmac.compare_digest

members.name: CI check for skill and agent frontmatter
members.problem: Skill files can rot silently: a missing name, a name that differs from its folder, a stale Alembic head literal.
members.mechanism: Keep the one-off gate from commit 1ac6b15 as a Node CI step: fatal on SKILL.md frontmatter (name equals folder, description present and at most 1024 chars) and agent fields; flag a stale head literal; slash-path citations warn only.
members.status_note: Adopted in the sweep; to be added to P1-ci or P1. Not yet built.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Local GPU speech-to-text for blocked recordings
members.problem: YouTube blocks caption requests from this machine's address, so talks cannot be read.
members.mechanism: Download audio-only streams and transcribe with faster-whisper distil-large-v3 through an ephemeral uv run environment on the RTX 5070. Nothing is installed system-wide.
members.status_note: Used for nine recordings in the addendum.
members.results: 9 recordings, about 7 hours, 172 MB, transcribed in about 12 minutes on GPU at 19-45x real time (M); CPU with other sessions loading: 2.7x (M).

members.name: Podcast RSS feeds for transcripts
members.problem: Show pages expose only part of a podcast's transcript.
members.mechanism: Read the RSS feed's transcript tag (Tessl's feed had the full text in four formats); else fetch the MP3 enclosure.
members.status_note: Used for Tessl 124 and Build Wiz.
members.results: Tessl: full 12,100-word transcript vs 1,800 words from the site (M).

members.name: Separate Postgres 17 restore stack for evidence
members.problem: Restoring a production dump into the test database or an older Postgres could mix evidence with test state or fail.
members.mechanism: A dump is restored into its own Postgres 17 container, never the test database; completeness is measured with exact counts per table, not estimates; a fixed read-only query set (Appendix B) is run.
members.status_note: Only used if W0 produces a dump.
members.results: not yet tested

members.problem: Behaviour-changing PRs deploy together at P4c, and a first untested sequence could damage the restored production data.
members.mechanism: For each behaviour-changing PR that reaches main: restore the newest dump into Postgres 17, run start.sh's migrations to the new head, run the PR's post-deploy check, and record a rehearsal row beside its deploy-train row.
members.status_note: Not started; wave C.
members.results: Not yet tested.

members.name: Owner delegates merging and starts to the coordinator
members.problem: Waiting for the owner to approve every merge and next-slice start would slow a parallel program and stall work while he is away.
members.mechanism: The root or coordinator merges and starts next slices itself. FixFlow rule: squash-merge when CI is green on the head, its own binding review passed on that SHA, the PR is not on the merge-hold list and its predecessor is merged. Merging deploys nothing. Archiving still needs the owner's word.
members.status_note: In use in the clinic testbed (does not survive the owner's absence); recorded for FixFlow as a W0-results decision row, no PR merged under it yet in the sources.
members.results: Clinic: no numbers (M: none); the usage limit plus the start-on-owner-turn rule halted work on 6 Nov for three days (B03). FixFlow: no PR merged under the rule yet.
members.aka: owner delegates merge, A1-09, Owner-delegated autonomy for the orchestrator

members.name: Merge queue that refuses a wrong head
members.problem: Merges happen without anyone reading the final head (5 of 6 high-risk merges, M); the root merged and edited the board by hand.
members.mechanism: A local script merges one at a time under a lock, runs one check on the merged result, confirms the typed verdict's head SHA equals the merged head, requires a reader field (refuses 'none' or 'own' on high-risk), applies the generated board diff and flags a dirty worktree. Record-only first.
members.status_note: Phase 3 mechanism 6; sources rated trial. Refusal is an owner decision: some unread heads of 10 November followed the owner's instruction to merge on session reports.
members.results: Not yet run. Must flag the unread heads of 10 and 11 Nov on replay over 65 merges (M). Target: unread high-risk final heads from 5 of 6 (M) to zero (T).
members.aka: Mechanism 6, B2 The serial gate, G2-F118, G4-F232, G1-F196, G2-F041, G4-F068

members.problem: Decisions made mid-phase live only in chat, and a summary after compaction can lose or distort them.
members.mechanism: Each draft PR body carries a 'Decisions / ruled out / owner corrections (this phase)' list, appended when each event occurs, so a fresh session recovers them from the repository.
